# Process Architecture L0 — Procurement

> **L0-Procurement** · level 0 · the enterprise process framework

The enterprise procurement process framework. Twenty-five processes across six domains, expressed as text-first process objects that are versioned in Git, published through the management system, and served to AI agents over MCP with explicit delegation boundaries.

---

## Purpose

This framework is the connective tissue of procurement: it links what the enterprise intends (strategy, policies) to what happens (processes), to how it is judged (skills), to what is produced (templates), and it makes every one of those things legible to an AI agent with a defined and auditable mandate.

## Why the hierarchy matters

The procurement framework is organised as **one L0 domain → six L1 domains → twenty-five L2 processes**. The levels are not documentation decoration: each level carries a different granularity of decision and a different AI delegation ceiling, so an agent that knows where it is in the hierarchy knows how much freedom it has.

| Level | Artefact | Granularity | AI ceiling | Typical reader |
|-------|----------|-------------|-----------|----------------|
| L0 | Process architecture | The whole domain | L1 | Executive, auditor |
| L1 | Domain architecture | A coherent slice of the domain | L2 | Domain lead, category manager |
| L2 | Process object | An executable process | L3 within mandate | Practitioner, agent |
| Step | Step directive | A single task | L4 for judgement steps | Whoever executes it |

## Level 1 domains

| ID | Code | Domain | Processes | AI ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L1-StrategyPerformance | SP | Strategy and Performance | 7 | L1 |
| L1-IntakeManagement | IM | Intake Management | 2 | L2 |
| L1-SourceToContract | S2C | Source to Contract | 5 | L2 |
| L1-PurchaseToOrder | PR2PO | Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order | 3 | L3 |
| L1-InvoiceToPay | I2P | Invoice to Pay | 4 | L2 |
| L1-SupplierManagement | SM | Supplier Management | 4 | L2 |

## End-to-end map

```text
Procurement (L0)
│
├ SP   Strategy and Performance ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│     1.1 Align Global Strategy        1.2 Align Category Strategy             │
│     1.3 Manage Risk                   1.4 Manage Procurement Improvements    │
│     1.5 Manage Savings Funnel         1.6 Manage Re-Negotiations             │
│     1.7 Govern Sustainability and ESG                                        │
│                                                                              │
├ IM   Intake Management ─────────  ┐                                          │
│     2.1 Request to Buying Channel │                                          │
│     2.2 Demand Management ────────┼──► S2C ──► PR2PO ──► I2P                 │
│                                   │    │                                     │
│                                   │    │       │         │                   │
├ S2C  Source to Contract ──────────┘    │       │         │                   │
│     3.1 Sourcing                       │       │         │                   │
│     3.2 Awarding                       ▼       ▼         ▼                   │
│     3.3 Contracting                    (sign)  (PO)      (Invoice)           │
│     3.4 Govern Inventory and Material Master                                 │
│     3.5 Transaction Enablement                                               │
│                                                          │                   │
├ SM   Supplier Management ────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┘
│     6.1 Onboard   6.2 Qualify   6.3 Offboard   6.4 Performance               │
│                                                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         cross-cutting: policies · skills · templates · AI delegation · audit
```

## Cross-domain flows

| Flow | From | To | Handover artefact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Demand to spend | Intake Management | Source to Contract | Qualified requisition with approved sourcing strategy |
| Award to transaction | Source to Contract | Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order | Executed contract, enriched master data and the rules to transact on it |
| Strategy to demand | Strategy and Performance | Intake Management | Category strategy and demand management rules |
| Spend to cash out | Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order | Invoice to Pay | Purchase order, receipt and invoice |
| Supplier lifecycle | Supplier Management | Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order | Qualified, transactable supplier master record |

## Enterprise KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Process digitalisation | Share of framework processes with a published, machine-readable process object | 100% |
| AI-eligible cycle time | Share of process steps executed end-to-end by an agent within its delegation | > 60% |
| Framework adoption | Active practitioners contributing to the framework per quarter | > 50 |
| Audit readiness | Share of AI-executed steps with complete evidence records | 100% |

## Enterprise risks

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| The framework becomes documentation nobody updates | Every change is a pull request; every process has a named owner and a review date that the tooling enforces |
| AI acts outside the framework because no machine-readable version existed | The MCP server serves only published, validated process objects |

## Delegation at enterprise level

```yaml
default_level: L1
authority: observe
data_classification: internal
decision_space:
  may_select: []
  must_select_from: []
  thresholds: {}
  prohibited:
    - act_outside_published_process
    - modify_process_during_execution
  escalation_band: null
constraints:
  - process_status_active
  - delegation_within_ceiling
guardrails:
  - policy_ai_delegation_of_record
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: always
reversible: true
evidence:
  - process_version_at_execution
  - agent_decision_log
```

# Intake Management

> **IM** · L1-IntakeManagement · level 1 domain

Captures every demand for goods and services at the point of origin, qualifies it against strategy and budget, and routes it to the right buying channel — so that only valid, funded, approved requests reach sourcing.

---

## Purpose

Intake Management is the front door of procurement. It exists to stop three specific failures: buying what the business already has, buying without a funding decision, and buying outside the approved channel. It is also where the majority of avoidable sourcing cycles are eliminated.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Guided intake of purchase requirements from any function
- Catalogue and contract-first recommendation
- Demand consolidation and de-duplication
- Qualification against category strategy, budget and approval thresholds
- Routing to sourcing, catalogue purchase, or rejection

**Out of scope**

- Category strategy definition (Proc_1.2)
- Sourcing event execution (Proc_3.1)
- Requisition approval (Proc_4.1)

## Entry criteria

- Category strategy published for the requested category
- Budget lines loaded for the requesting function

## Exit criteria

- Request qualified and routed to a buying channel
- Rejection reasons recorded where applicable

## Processes in this domain

| ID | Process | Purpose | AI ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proc_2.1 | Request to Buying Channel | Captures a purchase requirement, qualifies it against strategy, budget and thresholds, matches it to existing catalogue and contract supply, and routes it to the correct buying channel — or rejects it with a reason | L3 |
| Proc_2.2 | Demand Management | Consolidates, de-duplicates, analyses and shapes demand across the enterprise so that sourcing runs against a clear, aggregated picture rather than a stream of isolated requests | L3 |

## Flow

```text
Intake Management (IM)
  ├─ 2.1 Request to Buying Channel → guided capture → catalogue match → qualification → routing decision
  └─ 2.2 Demand Management        → consolidation, de-duplication, aggregate view, demand shaping
       (2.1 output feeds 2.2; 2.2 output is the qualified, prioritised demand fed to S2C)
```

## Systems

| System | Role in this domain | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coupa Intake | Guided intake and requisition capture | coupa |
| Coupa Procurement | Requisition to purchase order | coupa |
| SAP S/4HANA | Financial and operational ledger | erp |
| Microsoft Teams | Collaboration and approvals | collaboration |

## Domain delegation profile

```yaml
default_level: L2
authority: prepare
data_classification: internal
decision_space:
  may_select: []
  must_select_from: []
  thresholds: {}
  prohibited:
    - approve_own_requisition
    - split_request_to_bypass_threshold
  escalation_band: null
constraints:
  - requester_authenticated
  - budget_period_open
guardrails:
  - policy_catalog_first
  - policy_thresholds_and_approvals
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: required
reversible: true
evidence:
  - intake_decision_log
  - routing_decision
```

## Domain KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intake to requisition conversion | Share of intake requests that become a requisition rather than being rejected or abandoned | > 70% |
| Catalogue hit rate | Share of intake requests resolved from an approved catalogue | > 45% |
| Requisition touch time | Elapsed time from intake submission to approved requisition | < 2 business days |

## Risks

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Requests are split across intakes to stay below approval thresholds | Detect and consolidate split requests at the requester level and refer them for review |
| Buyers are bypassed through informal channels | Catalogue-first routing and block payment for spend without a compliant requisition |

# Invoice to Pay

> **I2P** · L1-InvoiceToPay · level 1 domain

Receives supplier invoices, matches them against the purchase order and receipt, resolves exceptions, and releases payment — with a proportionate, always-on control against duplicate and fraudulent payment.

---

## Purpose

Invoice to Pay is where the organisation either captures or loses the value negotiated upstream. The design goal is that the happy path is entirely automated and exception-free, and that every exception is handled by a human with the context to resolve it quickly.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Invoice capture from all channels including e-invoicing
- Duplicate, fraud and sanctions screening
- Three-way match and tolerance handling
- Exception resolution and recovery
- Payment scheduling and release

**Out of scope**

- Purchase order creation (Proc_4.2)
- Goods receipt confirmation (Proc_4.3)
- Supplier commercial terms renegotiation (Proc_1.6)

## Entry criteria

- PO issued (or a documented non-PO basis)
- Supplier banking data validated and current

## Exit criteria

- Payment released and remittance sent
- Invoice and payment evidence archived

## Processes in this domain

| ID | Process | Purpose | AI ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proc_5.1 | Receive Invoice | Captures supplier invoices from every channel, validates their structure, screens them for duplication, fraud and sanctions exposure, and routes them into the matching process | L2 |
| Proc_5.2 | Match and Approve Invoice | Matches the invoice against the purchase order and the goods receipt, evaluates variances against defined tolerances, routes the invoice for approval, and releases it into the payment run | L3 |
| Proc_5.3 | Resolve Invoice Issue | Classifies invoice exceptions, assigns them to the right owner with the context to act, resolves them — by correcting, disputing, writing off or cancelling — and feeds the recurring root cause back into process improvement | L2 |
| Proc_5.4 | Pay Invoice | Schedules approved invoices into payment runs, applies early-payment discounts and run optimisations, verifies supplier banking data independently, releases payment and sends remittance advice | L2 |

## Flow

```text
Invoice to Pay (I2P)
  ├─ 5.1 Receive Invoice        → capture → screening → duplicate check → routing
  ├─ 5.2 Match and Approve Invoice → 3-way match → tolerance evaluation → approval
  ├─ 5.3 Resolve Invoice Issue  → exception classification → assignment → resolution → re-match
  └─ 5.4 Pay Invoice            → payment run → release → remittance → archiving
```

## Systems

| System | Role in this domain | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coupa Invoicing | Invoice capture, matching, exceptions | coupa |
| SAP S/4HANA | Financial and operational ledger | erp |
| SAP Tax Management | Determination and tax compliance | finance |
| Microsoft Teams | Collaboration and approvals | collaboration |

## Domain delegation profile

```yaml
default_level: L2
authority: prepare
data_classification: confidential
decision_space:
  may_select: []
  must_select_from: []
  thresholds: {}
  prohibited:
    - release_payment_without_match
    - change_bank_details
    - waive_match_tolerance
  escalation_band: null
constraints:
  - po_exists_or_exception_approved
  - supplier_bank_verified
guardrails:
  - policy_fraud_and_duplicate_control
  - policy_thresholds_and_approvals
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: required
reversible: false
evidence:
  - match_result
  - exception_reason
  - payment_release_log
```

## Domain KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Straight-through processing rate | Share of invoices paid without any human touch | > 80% |
| Cost per invoice | Total accounts payable operating cost divided by invoices processed | tracked, trending down |
| Exception resolution time | Elapsed working days from invoice submission to exception cleared | < 5 days |

## Risks

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Payment redirection fraud via changed bank details | Dual-channel verification of bank changes, independent of the change requester |
| Duplicate invoices paid twice | Probabilistic duplicate detection plus a duplicate invoice hold list |

# Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order

> **PR2PO** · L1-PurchaseToOrder · level 1 domain

Turns an approved requisition into a valid purchase order: verifies budget, obtains the right approvals, applies contract pricing, and issues the order with complete and accurate data.

---

## Purpose

This domain contains the highest-volume, most rules-bound process in procurement, which makes it the best early target for delegation at L3. Its objective is that every PO is complete on issue — because every downstream matching failure and every supplier complaint traces back to incomplete PO data.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Requisition review and budget validation
- Approval routing and delegation handling
- Catalogue and contract price application
- Purchase order creation, validation and issue
- PO amendment and change control

**Out of scope**

- Sourcing of non-catalogue items (Proc_3.1)
- Goods receipt (Proc_4.3)
- Supplier master creation (Proc_6.1)

## Entry criteria

- Requisition approved
- Supplier active and contract-covered where applicable

## Exit criteria

- PO issued and transmitted to supplier
- PO data complete to the master-data standard

## Processes in this domain

| ID | Process | Purpose | AI ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proc_4.1 | Approve Purchase Requisition | Validates a qualified requisition for completeness, budget and contract coverage, routes it to the right approver according to the threshold matrix, and releases it for purchase order creation | L3 |
| Proc_4.2 | Create and Distribute Purchase Order | Builds, validates, approves and issues the purchase order against an approved requisition, applying contract pricing and complete master data, then transmits the order to the supplier | L3 |
| Proc_4.3 | Receive Materials and Services | Confirms the arrival and acceptance of purchased materials and services, records the receipt in the transactional system, resolves variances, and completes the purchase order so that invoices can be matched | L3 |

## Flow

```text
Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order (PR2PO)
  ├─ 4.1 Approve Purchase Requisition → validate completeness → budget check → approval routing → release
  └─ 4.2 Create and Distribute Purchase Order → contract price → PO build → validation → issue → transmit
       (4.3 Receive Materials and Services closes the loop against 4.2)
```

## Systems

| System | Role in this domain | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coupa Procurement | Requisition to purchase order | coupa |
| SAP S/4HANA | Financial and operational ledger | erp |
| SAP Ariba Business Network | Supplier transactions and collaboration | srm |
| Microsoft Teams | Collaboration and approvals | collaboration |

## Domain delegation profile

```yaml

authority: execute
data_classification: internal
decision_space:
  may_select: []
  must_select_from: []

    po_value_eur: 25000

    - split_po_to_bypass_approval
    - amend_po_after_invoice_without_approval
  escalation_band: null
constraints:
  - requisition_approved
  - supplier_active
  - budget_available
guardrails:
  - policy_thresholds_and_approvals
  - policy_segregation_of_duties
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: on_exception
reversible: false
evidence:
  - po_issue_log
  - price_application_log
```

## Domain KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requisition to PO cycle time | Elapsed working hours from approved requisition to PO issue | < 4 hours |
| PO first-time-right | Share of POs issued without a subsequent correction, amendment or rejection | > 97% |

| Orders are placed outside contracts, losing negotiated prices | Contract coverage check is a blocking validation on PO creation |
| Buyers bypass the approval matrix by splitting POs | Aggregation of related requisitions within a rolling window before threshold evaluation |

# Source to Contract

> **S2C** · L1-SourceToContract · level 1 domain

Runs the competitive process from requirement analysis through sourcing event, award decision and contract formation — with the strategy, policies and evaluation criteria declared up front and enforced in real time.

---

## Purpose

Source to Contract is where competition and compliance actually happen. Its objective is a defensible award: a documented requirement, a fair and transparent event, an evaluation traceable to pre-declared criteria, and a contract that matches the award.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Requirement analysis and sourcing strategy
- Supplier market analysis and approach
- RFx creation, publication and management
- Bid evaluation and award recommendation
- Contract drafting, negotiation and execution
- Material master ownership, quality status and ordering rules
- Transaction enablement from the executed contract and the governed master data

**Out of scope**

- Requisition creation (Proc_4.1)
- Purchase order issuance (Proc_4.2)
- Post-award supplier performance management (Proc_6.4)

## Entry criteria

- Qualified demand from Intake Management
- Approved sourcing strategy
- Budget confirmed for the event

## Exit criteria

- Award decision approved and recorded
- Contract executed or a documented decision not to contract

## Processes in this domain

| ID | Process | Purpose | AI ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proc_3.1 | Sourcing | Turns a qualified requirement into a published, competitive sourcing event: requirement analysis, market analysis, sourcing strategy, approved shortlist, RFx authoring, review and publication | L2 |
| Proc_3.2 | Awarding | Evaluates bids against the pre-declared criteria, produces a traceable award recommendation, obtains the approvals required by policy, notifies bidders and records the award into the savings funnel | L2 |
| Proc_3.3 | Contracting | Converts an approved award into an executed, compliant contract: template selection, drafting from award terms, legal and commercial review, negotiation, signature, activation and obligation tracking | L2 |
| Proc_3.4 | Govern Inventory and Material Master | Governs the material master: ownership, quality status and the rules that decide which material may be ordered against which contract | L2 |
| Proc_3.5 | Transaction Enablement | Turns the executed contract and the governed master data into the transactions that can run: order, delivery, invoice and payment readiness | L2 |

## Flow

```text
Source to Contract (S2C)
  ├─ 3.1 Sourcing    → requirement analysis → market analysis → strategy → shortlist → RFx → publication
  ├─ 3.2 Awarding    → bid evaluation → clarification → award recommendation → approvals → award notification
  ├─ 3.3 Contracting → contract drafting → negotiation → legal review → signature → activation
  ├─ 3.4 Govern Inventory and Material Master → ownership → quality status → ordering rules
  └─ 3.5 Transaction Enablement → order → delivery → invoice → payment readiness
```

## Systems

| System | Role in this domain | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SAP Ariba Sourcing | Sourcing events, RFx, bid evaluation | e-procurement |
| Ivalua CLM | Contract lifecycle and obligations | other |
| DocuSign | Electronic signature | other |
| SAP S/4HANA | Financial and operational ledger | erp |

## Domain delegation profile

```yaml
default_level: L2
authority: prepare
data_classification: confidential
decision_space:
  may_select: []
  must_select_from: []
  thresholds: {}
  prohibited:
    - publish_rfx_without_approval
    - disclose_other_bid_pricing
    - award_to_unapproved_supplier
  escalation_band: null
constraints:
  - sourcing_strategy_approved
  - budget_confirmed
guardrails:
  - policy_competitive_tendering
  - policy_segregation_of_duties
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: required
reversible: false
evidence:
  - rfx_publication_log
  - evaluation_scorecard
  - award_decision_record
```

## Domain KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cycle time — requisition to award | Elapsed working days from approved requisition to award approval | < 35 days |
| Competitive bidding rate | Share of spend awarded via a competitive event where more than one bid was received | > 70% |
| Sourcing cost avoidance | Value of awards versus pre-event benchmark | > 6% |

## Risks

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Evaluation criteria are changed after bids are received | Criteria are locked at publication; any change voids the event and requires re-issue |
| Single-bid awards without documented justification | Single-bid justification is mandatory and approved at the same level as the award |

# Strategy and Performance

> **SP** · L1-StrategyPerformance · level 1 domain

Aligns procurement with enterprise strategy, manages risk, measures performance, controls the savings funnel and owns sustainability governance across the procurement portfolio.

---

## Purpose

Strategy and Performance converts enterprise objectives into procurement plans and keeps the function honest. It answers three questions continuously: are we buying the right things, are we managing the risks we said we would manage, and can we evidence the value procurement delivers?

## Scope

**In scope**

- Category and portfolio strategy aligned to enterprise objectives
- Procurement risk register, including third-party and concentration risk
- Savings funnel definition, validation and realisation reporting
- Re-negotiation and contract renewal planning
- Sustainability and ESG goals applied to sourcing decisions
- Process maturity improvement backlog

**Out of scope**

- Tactical execution of sourcing events (Proc_3.1)
- Transaction processing (Proc_4.x, Proc_5.x)
- Supplier master data maintenance (Proc_6.1)

## Entry criteria

- Enterprise objectives and budget envelope published for the fiscal year
- Category taxonomy and spend cube defined
- Named Category Directors for each category in scope

## Exit criteria

- Category strategies approved and published
- Risk register baselined with owners
- Savings funnel reconciled to finance baseline

## Processes in this domain

| ID | Process | Purpose | AI ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proc_1.1 | Align Global Strategy | Translates enterprise objectives into a procurement strategy: the value procurement will create, the categories in scope, the spend under management and the levers available to deliver it | L2 |
| Proc_1.2 | Align Category Strategy | Builds the executable strategy for a single category: demand profile, supplier base, sourcing levers, savings plan, risk exposure and the review calendar that keeps it alive | L1 |
| Proc_1.3 | Manage Risk | Maintains the procurement risk register: identification, assessment, mitigation and escalation of third-party, concentration, continuity, compliance and ESG risks across the supplier portfolio | L2 |
| Proc_1.4 | Manage Procurement Improvements | Turns operational evidence — cycle times, exception rates, leakage, agent performance — into a prioritised backlog of improvements to the process framework itself, and into published framework releases | L2 |
| Proc_1.5 | Manage Savings Funnel | Defines, validates, tracks and reports the savings funnel — from identified opportunity through to finance-validated realised savings — and detects leakage at every stage | L1 |
| Proc_1.6 | Manage Re-Negotiations | Runs the re-negotiation cycle: build the renewal calendar, benchmark current pricing, prepare and execute the re-negotiation, and capture the price-down back into contracts and catalogue pricing | L2 |
| Proc_1.7 | Govern Sustainability and ESG | Sets and enforces sustainability and ESG expectations across the supplier base: targets, supplier data collection, assessment, green sourcing levers, claims verification and disclosure | L2 |

## Flow

```text
Strategy and Performance (SP)
  ├─ 1.1 Align Global Strategy        → sets portfolio direction, category boundaries, target spend
  ├─ 1.2 Align Category Strategy       → per category: demand, sourcing levers, savings plan, risk profile
  ├─ 1.3 Manage Risk                   → third-party, concentration, ESG, continuity, compliance risk register
  ├─ 1.4 Manage Procurement Improvements → process maturity, cycle-time reduction, automation backlog
  ├─ 1.5 Manage Savings Funnel         → pipeline definition, validation, realisation tracking, leakage detection
  ├─ 1.6 Manage Re-Negotiations        → renewal calendar, benchmark-driven re-negotiation, price-down capture
  └─ 1.7 Govern Sustainability and ESG  → scope 1-3 targets, supplier ESG data, green sourcing levers
```

## Systems

| System | Role in this domain | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coupa SpendIQ Analytics | Spend classification and savings tracking | data |
| SAP BW | Reporting and dashboards | data |
| Microsoft Teams | Collaboration and approvals | collaboration |

## Domain delegation profile

```yaml
default_level: L1
authority: draft
data_classification: internal
decision_space:
  may_select: []
  must_select_from: []
  thresholds: {}
  prohibited:
    - set_corporate_target
    - commit_savings_to_finance
  escalation_band: null
constraints:
  - enterprise_objectives_published
  - spend_cube_loaded
guardrails:
  - policy_procurement_policy_of_record
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: required
reversible: true
evidence:
  - strategy_version
  - approval_record
```

## Domain KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Addressable spend coverage | Share of addressable spend covered by an approved category strategy | > 80% |
| Realised savings vs plan | Finance-validated savings realised against the category strategy plan | > 90% of plan |
| Contract coverage | Spend under an active contract or framework agreement | > 95% |
| Third-party risk closure | High-rated third-party risks closed within the agreed remediation window | > 90% |

## Risks

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Strategy is authored centrally and ignored by practitioners | Every strategy requires named practitioner co-authors and a co-design review before approval |
| Savings reported by procurement are not validated by finance | Dual validation by category finance before any savings enters the funnel |

# Supplier Management

> **SM** · L1-SupplierManagement · level 1 domain

Owns the supplier lifecycle — onboarding into systems, qualification, performance management and offboarding — and the master data that every other procurement process depends on.

---

## Purpose

Supplier Management is the domain that other domains depend on. If the supplier master is wrong, every downstream price, term and match is wrong. This domain therefore treats master data quality as a controlled artefact and performance management as a continuous, evidence-based practice rather than an annual survey.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Supplier onboarding, due diligence and system registration
- Supplier qualification and approval to transact
- Supplier performance measurement and development
- Supplier offboarding and blocklisting
- Supplier master data quality ownership

**Out of scope**

- Strategic sourcing and award (Proc_3.x)
- Payment execution (Proc_5.4)
- Product quality management in the business

## Entry criteria

- Supplier identified as a required trading partner
- Business sponsorship for the relationship

## Exit criteria

- Supplier active, qualified and monitored — or offboarded and archived

## Processes in this domain

| ID | Process | Purpose | AI ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Proc_6.1 | Onboard Supplier in Systems | Takes a prospective supplier through due diligence, risk assessment, master data creation and activation, so that only a verified, transactable supplier can receive orders or payments | L2 |
| Proc_6.2 | Qualify Supplier | Tests a supplier against the qualification criteria for its category — capability, capacity, quality, financial standing and compliance — and grants or withholds approval to transact and to be considered in sourcing | L4 |
| Proc_6.3 | Offboard Supplier | Detects the conditions that end a supplier relationship, blocks transactions, resolves open commitments, revokes access, handles data retention and archiving, and confirms the outcome | L2 |
| Proc_6.4 | Manage Supplier Performance | Measures supplier performance against contracted service levels and commercial outcomes, reviews it with the supplier, agrees development or corrective action, and feeds the results back into sourcing strategy and renewal decisions | L2 |

## Flow

```text
Supplier Management (SM)
  ├─ 6.1 Onboard Supplier in Systems → application → due diligence → master creation → activation
  ├─ 6.2 Qualify Supplier        → qualification criteria → assessment → approval to transact
  ├─ 6.3 Offboard Supplier       → trigger detection → transactional block → data purge/archive → attestation
  └─ 6.4 Manage Supplier Performance → scorecard → review → development plan → escalation
```

## Systems

| System | Role in this domain | Category |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SAP Ariba Supplier Management | Supplier onboarding and qualification | srm |
| SAP Ariba Business Network | Supplier transactions and collaboration | srm |
| SAP Supplier Performance Management | Supplier scorecards and development | srm |
| SAP S/4HANA | Financial and operational ledger | erp |
| SAP Quality Management | Supplier quality and audits | other |

## Domain delegation profile

```yaml
default_level: L2
authority: prepare
data_classification: confidential
decision_space:
  may_select: []
  must_select_from: []
  thresholds: {}
  prohibited:
    - activate_supplier_without_due_diligence
    - unblock_blocklisted_supplier
    - modify_verified_bank_data
  escalation_band: null
constraints:
  - due_diligence_complete
  - sponsor_named
guardrails:
  - policy_supplier_onboarding
  - policy_master_data_quality
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: required
reversible: true
evidence:
  - onboarding_record
  - qualification_decision
  - performance_snapshot
```

## Domain KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Onboarding lead time | Elapsed working days from supplier application to approved and transactable | < 10 days |
| Supplier master accuracy | Share of active supplier records passing the data quality ruleset | > 97% |
| Performance review coverage | Share of strategic suppliers with a current performance assessment | > 95% |

## Risks

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Suppliers transact before due diligence completes | The system blocks transactional status until every mandatory due-diligence artefact is present |
| Offboarding is missed, leaving suppliers able to transact and receive data | Offboarding triggered by contract end, performance failure or risk event, with a quarterly attestation |

title: AI Delegation Matrix
summary: The canonical definition of how much freedom an AI agent is granted to perform a task and make decisions. Every process, skill and template in this framework declares a delegation level. This document is the authority those declarations resolve against.
text: AI Delegation Matrix Why this exists. "AI may assist in procurement" is not a mandate. A mandate is actionable , bounded , enforceable and auditable . This document supplies the vocabulary for all four. If a step in this framework does not declare a delegation level, the process is not deployable — the validator rejects it. --- 1. The five delegation levels Levels describe who decides , not how much the AI is used. Level Name The AI may The human must Typical spend exposure ------- ------ ------------- --------------- ----------------------- L0 Observe Read, classify, extract, summarise, compare, flag Decide and act Any L1 Draft Produce a draft artefact for a human to edit and approve Review, edit, approve, execute Any L2 Execute with approval Perform system actions in a sandbox, then wait at a named checkpoint Approve at the checkpoint Bounded L3 Execute within mandate Perform system actions autonomously inside hard thresholds Monitor, and review the audit log Bounded and pre-authorised L4 Decide Make a bounded judgement call from a defined candidate set Audit, and periodically review the decision space Bounded, discretionary band The ceiling rule. The effective level of any step is the minimum of: A process can only ever narrow the delegation granted by the organisation-wide policy; it can never widen it. framework/policies/policy ai delegation of record.md sets the organisational ceilings. --- 2. Authority verbs Every delegation declaration pairs a level with an authority verb . The verb is what appears in the audit log and what the MCP server reports to a calling agent. Verb Meaning Reversible? ------ --------- ------------- observe Read-only. No state change anywhere. n/a draft Produces an artefact (text, table, proposal). No transaction. Yes — discard recommend Produces a ranked recommendation with rationale. No transaction. Yes — discard prepare Stages a transaction (e.g. creates a PO in draft) without submitting. Yes — cancel execute Submits a transaction that changes state. Only if the domain supports reversal decide Selects among candidate options and commits to one. Only if reversible by policy Irreversibility is the real risk boundary. An execute step that charges a supplier's bank account is not equivalent to one that writes a draft to a staging area. The reversible flag is therefore mandatory and is checked by the validator. --- 3. The decision space The decision space is the bounded set of choices an agent is permitted to make. It is expressed as four orthogonal controls: Four rules govern the decision space: 1. Closed sets. must select from is closed. If the agent cannot find an acceptable candidate inside the set, it must escalate — it must never widen the set itself. 2. Numeric thresholds decide autonomy. If a threshold applies to the step, the agent is L3 below the threshold and L2 above it. Threshold crossing is evaluated before the action, never after. 3. Prohibited is absolute. prohibited is not a default suggestion. It is enforced by the policy gateway before the action is dispatched. 4. Escalation band is a subset of prohibited ambiguity. If the agent is unsure whether a value falls inside or outside the band, it escalates. --- 4. Constraints, guardrails, escalation Three different things, three different enforcement points: Element Question it answers Enforced by When --------- -------------------- -------------- ------ constraints What must be true for this step to run at all? Pre-flight validator Before the step starts guardrails Which policies and controls constrain the action? Policy gateway Before every action escalation When does the agent hand control back to a human? Orchestrator Continuously Escalation is a first-class outcome. An agent that escalates has succeeded at its job. Systems that punish escalation produce agents that guess — the single largest source of governance risk in agentic procurement. --- 5. Evidence and audit Delegation without evidence is delegation without accountability. Every step that declares execute or decide must declare the evidence it produces: The audit record is what lets the process-auditing companion propose improvements later, and what lets an external AI agent's decisions be re-examined months afterwards. --- 6. Data classification ceiling An agent may never process data above the classification ceiling of the step it is acting in, regardless of its capability or the level granted. Classification Typical content Autonomous agent permitted? ---------------- ----------------- ----------------------------- public Published tender notices, supplier websites Yes, up to L3 internal Process definitions, playbooks, internal KPIs Yes, up to L3 confidential Supplier pricing, contract terms, negotiation positions L2 maximum unless explicitly mandated restricted Personal data, national-security-adjacent data, M&A targets L1 maximum — always a human restricted is a hard stop. No delegation level, no mandate and no exception may authorise an autonomous agent to act on restricted data. This is the one rule in this matrix that cannot be overridden locally. --- 7. Setting the levels: who decides what Level change Who How -------------- ----- ----- Draft a process with a level Process owner + co-design community PR against the framework repo Raise a level within an existing mandate Delegation Review Board Delegation RFC, quarterly window Set an organisational ceiling Procurement Governance + Risk Change to policy ai delegation of record Emergency suspension of a level Any governance role Incident record + post-incident review Levels expire. A delegation granted at L3 without a review cadence and a reviewer is downgraded to L2 automatically by the validator. Delegation is a lease, not a permanent right — that is what keeps it honest. --- 8. Worked examples An agent triaging an invoice that does not match the PO → L0, Observe. It may read the PO, the invoice and the goods receipt, and flag a mismatch with a reason. It may not create a credit memo or contact the supplier. # AI Delegation Matrix

> **Why this exists.** "AI may assist in procurement" is not a mandate. A mandate is
> *actionable*, *bounded*, *enforceable* and *auditable*. This document supplies the
> vocabulary for all four. If a step in this framework does not declare a delegation
> level, the process is not deployable — the validator rejects it.

---

## 1. The five delegation levels

Levels describe **who decides**, not how much the AI is used.

| Level | Name | The AI may | The human must | Typical spend exposure |
|-------|------|-------------|---------------|-----------------------|
| **L0** | Observe | Read, classify, extract, summarise, compare, flag | Decide and act | Any |
| **L1** | Draft | Produce a draft artefact for a human to edit and approve | Review, edit, approve, execute | Any |
| **L2** | Execute with approval | Perform system actions in a sandbox, then wait at a named checkpoint | Approve at the checkpoint | Bounded |
| **L3** | Execute within mandate | Perform system actions autonomously inside hard thresholds | Monitor, and review the audit log | Bounded and pre-authorised |
| **L4** | Decide | Make a bounded judgement call from a defined candidate set | Audit, and periodically review the decision space | Bounded, discretionary band |

**The ceiling rule.** The effective level of any step is the *minimum* of:

```
effective_level = min(process.ai_delegation.default_level, step.ai.level)
```

A process can only ever *narrow* the delegation granted by the organisation-wide
policy; it can never widen it. `framework/policies/policy_ai_delegation_of_record.md`
sets the organisational ceilings.

---

## 2. Authority verbs

Every delegation declaration pairs a level with an **authority verb**. The verb is what
appears in the audit log and what the MCP server reports to a calling agent.

| Verb | Meaning | Reversible? |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `observe` | Read-only. No state change anywhere. | n/a |
| `draft` | Produces an artefact (text, table, proposal). No transaction. | Yes — discard |
| `recommend` | Produces a ranked recommendation with rationale. No transaction. | Yes — discard |
| `prepare` | Stages a transaction (e.g. creates a PO in draft) without submitting. | Yes — cancel |
| `execute` | Submits a transaction that changes state. | Only if the domain supports reversal |
| `decide` | Selects among candidate options and commits to one. | Only if reversible by policy |

> **Irreversibility is the real risk boundary.** An `execute` step that charges a
> supplier's bank account is not equivalent to one that writes a draft to a staging
> area. The `reversible` flag is therefore mandatory and is checked by the validator.

---

## 3. The decision space

The decision space is the **bounded set of choices** an agent is permitted to make.
It is expressed as four orthogonal controls:

```yaml
decision_space:
  may_select:            # what categories of option the agent may choose between
    - "approved_supplier_panel"
  must_select_from:      # hard candidate sets — the agent may not go outside these
    - "policy_approved_suppliers.candidate_set_id=cat_it_services"
  thresholds:            # numeric boundaries that partition L3/L4 space from L2
    contract_value_eur: 250000
    quote_deviation_pct: 10
  prohibited:            # actions the agent may never take at this step, at any level
    - "commit_spend"
    - "disclose_confidential_pricing_to_supplier"
  escalation_band:       # the score/risk band where the agent must hand back
    "supplier_risk_score > 0.6"
```

Four rules govern the decision space:

1. **Closed sets.** `must_select_from` is closed. If the agent cannot find an
   acceptable candidate inside the set, it *must* escalate — it must never
   widen the set itself.
2. **Numeric thresholds decide autonomy.** If a threshold applies to the step,
   the agent is L3 below the threshold and L2 above it. Threshold crossing is
   evaluated *before* the action, never after.
3. **Prohibited is absolute.** `prohibited` is not a default suggestion. It is
   enforced by the policy gateway before the action is dispatched.
4. **Escalation band is a subset of prohibited ambiguity.** If the agent is unsure
   whether a value falls inside or outside the band, it escalates.

---

## 4. Constraints, guardrails, escalation

Three different things, three different enforcement points:

| Element | Question it answers | Enforced by | When |
|---------|--------------------|--------------|------|
| `constraints` | *What must be true for this step to run at all?* | Pre-flight validator | Before the step starts |
| `guardrails` | *Which policies and controls constrain the action?* | Policy gateway | Before every action |
| `escalation` | *When does the agent hand control back to a human?* | Orchestrator | Continuously |

```yaml
constraints:
  - "sourcing_strategy_approved"
  - "budget_available_for_category"

guardrails:
  - "policy_competitive_tendering"
  - "policy_segregation_of_duties"

escalation:
  trigger: "qualified_bidders < 3"
  to: "Category Manager"
  sla_hours: 24
```

**Escalation is a first-class outcome.** An agent that escalates has *succeeded* at its
job. Systems that punish escalation produce agents that guess — the single largest
source of governance risk in agentic procurement.

---

## 5. Evidence and audit

Delegation without evidence is delegation without accountability. Every step that
declares `execute` or `decide` **must** declare the evidence it produces:

```yaml
evidence:
  - "rfp_publication_event_log"     # what happened
  - "decision_rationale"            # why it happened
  - "inputs_snapshot_hash"          # what it was based on
  - "agent_identity_and_model_version"
```

The audit record is what lets the process-auditing companion propose improvements
later, and what lets an external AI agent's decisions be re-examined months afterwards.

---

## 6. Data classification ceiling

An agent may never process data above the classification ceiling of the step it is
acting in, regardless of its capability or the level granted.

| Classification | Typical content | Autonomous agent permitted? |
|----------------|-----------------|-----------------------------|
| `public` | Published tender notices, supplier websites | Yes, up to L3 |
| `internal` | Process definitions, playbooks, internal KPIs | Yes, up to L3 |
| `confidential` | Supplier pricing, contract terms, negotiation positions | L2 maximum unless explicitly mandated |
| `restricted` | Personal data, national-security-adjacent data, M&A targets | **L1 maximum — always a human**

`restricted` is a hard stop. No delegation level, no mandate and no exception may
authorise an autonomous agent to act on restricted data. This is the one rule in this
matrix that cannot be overridden locally.

---

## 7. Setting the levels: who decides what

| Level change | Who | How |
|--------------|-----|-----|
| Draft a process with a level | Process owner + co-design community | PR against the framework repo |
| Raise a level within an existing mandate | Delegation Review Board | Delegation RFC, quarterly window |
| Set an organisational ceiling | Procurement Governance + Risk | Change to `policy_ai_delegation_of_record` |
| Emergency suspension of a level | Any governance role | Incident record + post-incident review |

**Levels expire.** A delegation granted at L3 without a `review_cadence` and a
`reviewer` is downgraded to L2 automatically by the validator. Delegation is a lease,
not a permanent right — that is what keeps it honest.

---

## 8. Worked examples

**An agent triaging an invoice that does not match the PO** → **L0, Observe.**
It may read the PO, the invoice and the goods receipt, and flag a mismatch with a
reason. It may not create a credit memo or contact the supplier. Why: the money
movement is irreversible and the reconciliation rules differ per category.

**An agent drafting an RfP from a category strategy** → **L1, Draft.**
It may assemble a draft RfP using the approved template and the category strategy.
A human must review before publication. Why: publication is externally visible and
competitively sensitive.

**An agent awarding a purchase order under a delegated authority** → **L3, Execute
within mandate**, bounded by `thresholds.contract_value_eur: 25000` and
`must_select_from: approved_supplier_panel`. Above the threshold it drops to L2 and
routes for approval. Why: low-value, high-volume, rule-bound decisions are where
automation pays and risk is lowest.

**An agent choosing between two qualified suppliers within a score band** → **L4,
Decide**, with `escalation_band: "supplier_risk_score > 0.6"`, mandatory
`evidence: [decision_rationale]`, and a monthly audit sample. Why: this is a genuine
judgement call, but it is bounded, and the reasoning is auditable.

---

## 9. How to read this from a process file

```yaml
# front matter of a process
ai_delegation:
  default_level: L2
  authority: prepare
  data_classification: confidential
  human_checkpoint: required
  reversible: true
```

```yaml
# inside a step
ai:
  level: L1
  authority: draft
  decision_space:
    must_select_from: [policy_approved_template_set]
    prohibited: [publish_without_approval]
  constraints: [sourcing_strategy_approved]
  guardrails: [policy_competitive_tendering]
  escalation:
    trigger: "scope_change_detected"
    to: "Procurement Business Partner"
    sla_hours: 8
  evidence: [draft_rfp_hash]
```

An external agent calling the MCP server receives both, plus the resolution rule
from §1. It therefore always knows — without asking — the ceiling it operates under.

---

- [`policy_ai_delegation_of_record`](../policies/policy_ai_delegation_of_record.md) — the organisational ceilings this matrix resolves against
- [`Control-Points.md`](./Control-Points.md) — where human approval is structurally required

# Control Points

A **control point** is a named place in the process where the AI agent must stop.
Control points are the mechanism that turns "AI-assisted procurement" into
"governed procurement". Every process in this framework inherits the control points
listed here unless it explicitly declares a stricter one.

| # | Control point | Process | AI ceiling | Human role | Reversible? |
|---|---------------|---------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| CP-1 | Strategy & demand approved | Proc_1.1 / Proc_2.1 | L1 | Category Manager | Yes |
| CP-2 | Sourcing strategy & event type chosen | Proc_3.1 | L2 | Procurement Business Partner | Yes |
| CP-3 | Supplier shortlist approved | Proc_3.1 → Proc_3.2 | L2 | Procurement Business Partner | Yes |
| CP-4 | Award decision signed off | Proc_3.2 | L2 | Delegated Approver | No |
| CP-5 | Contract terms agreed | Proc_3.3 | L2 | Legal + Procurement | No |
| CP-6 | Requisition approved | Proc_4.1 | L2 | Budget Owner | Partially |
| CP-7 | PO issued | Proc_4.2 | L3 under threshold | Delegated Approver | Partially |
| CP-8 | Goods receipt confirmed | Proc_4.3 | L2 | Receiver / Inventory | Partially |
| CP-9 | Invoice matched & approved | Proc_5.2 | L2 | Account Payable | Partially |
| CP-10 | Payment released | Proc_5.4 | L2 | Treasury / AP | No |
| CP-11 | Supplier onboarded to systems | Proc_6.1 | L2 | Supplier Master Data Owner | Yes |
| CP-12 | Supplier qualified | Proc_6.2 | L2 | Supplier Quality | Yes |
| CP-13 | Supplier offboarded | Proc_6.3 | L2 | Supplier Master Data Owner | Partially |
| CP-14 | Supplier removed from panel / blocklist | Proc_6.3 | L1 | Procurement Governance | Partially |

## Rules

1. **An agent may never pass a control point by itself at L3.** The highest ceiling
   at any control point is L3 *and only* where the row says so explicitly. Everywhere
   else, an agent must wait for the named human role.
2. **Segregation of duties is structural.** The role that prepares an artefact may
   never be the role that approves it. The validator checks this against the
   `roles` block of each process.
3. **A control point without an audit record does not exist.** Every control point
   produces an immutable event containing: actor identity, agent identity, input
   snapshot hash, decision, timestamp.
4. **Restricting a control point is a policy change, not a process edit.** It goes
   through the Delegation Review Board.

## Delegation Review Board

| Role | Member | Decision right |
|------|--------|----------------|
| Chair | Head of Procurement Governance | Ceilings, suspension |
| Member | Procurement Operations Lead | Process feasibility |
| Member | Finance Controller | Financial control points |
| Member | Legal Counsel | Contractual control points |
| Member | CISO / Data Protection Officer | Classification ceilings |
| Member | Category Manager (rotating) | Practitioner voice |

Cadence: quarterly review window, plus emergency sessions on incident.

# Glossary

The framework is only useful if the same word means the same thing in every
document. This is that list.

---

## The framework itself

**Process object** — the unit of the framework: a markdown file with structured
front matter (identity, ownership, taxonomy, inputs, outputs, relations, AI
delegation, audit) and a structured body (purpose, scope, steps, decision
criteria, policies, skills, templates, KPIs, risks, exceptions, change log).
The front matter is what a machine reads; the body is what a human reads. Both
live in one file so they cannot drift apart.

**L0 / L1 / L2** — the three levels of the hierarchy. *L0* is the enterprise
architecture: the whole map, the cross-domain flows, the enterprise KPIs. *L1*
is a domain: a coherent area of procurement with its own entry and exit
criteria, such as Source-to-Contract or Invoice-to-Pay. *L2* is a process: a
unit of work with a trigger, a defined output and a named owner. A step inside
a process is not a level — it is a directive.

**Hierarchy edge** — a containment relation. "Proc_4.1 is contained in
Purchase to Order, which is contained in the enterprise architecture."

**Flow edge** — a value flow. "A completed purchase order flows to Goods
Receipt." Flow edges point upstream to downstream, and they are what breaks
when information has to be chased by hand.

**Governs edge** — a constraint. "Policy X governs Proc_4.1", "Skill Y
governs Proc_3.2", "Template Z governs the artefact produced by Proc_5.3."

**Process Architecture L0** — the map of the whole framework, rendered as text
and as a graph. It is the answer to "where am I?"

---

## AI delegation

**AI Delegation Model (ADM)** — the framework's model of how much freedom an
agent has. Five levels, a decision space, three enforcement points and a rule
that escalation is a success.

**Level (L0–L4)** — how much freedom the agent has at a given step.

| Level | Name | The agent may |
|-------|------|---------------|
| L0 | Observe | Read, classify, summarise, flag. |
| L1 | Draft | Produce artefacts a human edits and approves. |
| L2 | Execute with approval | Act, but stop at a named human checkpoint. |
| L3 | Execute within mandate | Act autonomously inside hard thresholds. |
| L4 | Decide | Make a bounded judgement call from a closed candidate set. |

**Ceiling rule** — `effective = min(process ceiling, step level)`, hard-capped
at L1 for restricted data. A step can ask for more than its process allows; it
will not get it.

**Authority verb** — what the agent is permitted to *do*, as distinct from how
much freedom it has. The verbs are `observe`, `draft`, `recommend`, `prepare`,
`execute`, `decide`.

**Decision space** — the boundary of what the agent may decide: the candidate
set it may choose from, the numeric thresholds that decide its autonomy, the
actions that are prohibited outright, and the band in which it must escalate.

**Constraint** — a precondition checked before a step runs. "The requisition
is qualified." A constraint is about the world; a guardrail is about the act.

**Guardrail** — a policy check applied at the point of action, by the policy
gateway. "Do not issue a purchase order without a recorded approval."

**Escalation** — the hand-over route when a trigger fires. It names the target
role and the service level. Escalation is a **successful outcome**: an agent
that escalates has done its job, and the audit trail records the hand-over
rather than a failure.

**Human checkpoint** — the point at which a human must take over. `always`,
`required`, `on_exception` or `never`.

**Evidence** — the record that an action happened: what was done, under which
version of which policy, with which supporting artefacts. An action without
evidence did not happen.

**Data classification** — how sensitive the data is: `public`, `internal`,
`confidential` or `restricted`. The classification caps the level:
restricted is a hard stop at L1.

**Delegation Register** — the list of places in the framework where an agent
holds more than L2. A delegation above L2 is a **lease**, not a grant: it names
a reviewer, a review cadence, and the steps it covers, and it comes back to the
Delegation Review Board when the lease expires.

**Control point (CP-x)** — a named place in the value chain where an agent is
structurally required to stop. Fourteen of them, listed in
[`Control-Points.md`](./Control-Points.md).

**Delegation Review Board** — the body that grants, reviews and withdraws
delegations. Its composition and cadence are set out in the Control Points
document.

---

## Procurement

**Intake** — the request entering the organisation. The place where demand is
qualified against strategy, budget and thresholds before anything else
happens.

**Channel strategy** — the rule that decides whether a request is served from
the catalogue, from a contract, through a tender, or directly.

**Catalogue** — the pre-approved list of items or services that can be ordered
without a new sourcing event.

**Bid** — a supplier's response to a request for quotation or proposal.

**Three-way match** — the control that compares the invoice to the purchase
order and to the goods receipt before payment. The match itself is arithmetic;
the approval and the payment release are human.

**Goods receipt note (GRN)** — the record that goods or services were received.
It is the third leg of the three-way match.

**Service entry sheet (SES)** — the record that a service was received and
accepted, where no physical goods exist.

**Debit note** — a document that reduces an invoice rather than requesting
payment.

**Supplier risk** — the assessed likelihood and impact of a supplier failing to
deliver. Classified on a published scale, which is what makes it delegable.

**Conditional approval** — a supplier is approved to trade, with stated
conditions (volume caps, enhanced monitoring, a defined review date) rather
than being approved outright.

**Offboarding** — the controlled removal of a supplier from the active
population: no new orders, final invoices settled, personal and system access
revoked, master data archived.

**Material master** — the record that defines an item: its description, its
plant of record, its classification, the rules that govern it. Master data
quality is a procurement responsibility, not an IT one.

**ESIG / sustainability** — the environmental, social and governance criteria
applied to a category, a supplier or a contract.

---

## The toolchain

**Compiler** — the tool that reads the markdown and emits the graph, the index,
the search index and the manifest. It is deterministic: the same markdown
always produces the same artefacts.

**Validator** — the tool that refuses to build a framework that is internally
inconsistent: broken references, a step that exceeds its process ceiling, a
delegation above L2 with no lease, a decision with no evidence.

**MCP server** — the Model Context Protocol server that exposes the framework
to agents in other applications. Eleven tools, served over stdio. It is the
same read model the website uses.

**Management System** — the publishing surface. The *source of truth* is the
git repository; the Management System is what makes a published version
visible, auditable and citable to the organisation. It does not hold the
content — it holds the pointer to it and the record of who approved it.

# Agent Access to the Process Framework

> **policy_agent_access_and_mcp** · ai-governance policy · version 1.0.0

Governs how external and internal AI agents discover, read and act upon the process framework over MCP, including scoping, versioning, rate limits and audit.

---

## Purpose

Serving the framework over MCP is what turns it from documentation into infrastructure. That is exactly why access needs rules: an agent that can read the framework can also discover the delegation ceilings, the escalation routes and the templates — and therefore needs to be a known, scoped actor.

## Statement

All access to the process framework by an AI agent shall be authenticated, scoped to named processes and named tools, and logged. Agents shall be served only process objects with an active status. The framework version in force at the moment of execution shall be recorded with the resulting decision, so that any historical action can be replayed against the rules that applied at the time.

## Rules

- Every agent holds a scoped credential identifying the agent, its owner and its permitted tools.
- The MCP server serves only published, validated process objects with status `active`.
- Every tool response embeds the framework version and the delegation ceiling that applies.
- Agent queries are logged with the identity of the calling agent and the returned context.
- A supplier-side agent may be granted access to the supplier-facing subset only.
- Rate limits and context budgets apply per agent.

## Applies to

_None._

## Enforcement

```yaml
mode: pre_action
enforced_by:
  - mcp-gateway
  - auth-service
  - audit-log
on_violation: block
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: CISO
```

## Rationale

The version-in-force requirement is what makes the framework auditable. Without it, an action taken under last year's delegation cannot be judged against last year's rules — and the audit becomes opinion.

## Exceptions

_No exceptions are granted under this policy._

## Compliance evidence

- mcp_access_log
- framework_version_stamps
- agent_registry

# AI Delegation of Record

> **policy_ai_delegation_of_record** · ai-governance policy · version 1.0.0

Sets the organisational ceilings for AI delegation, the conditions under which each level may be granted, and the review and revocation mechanism that keeps delegation a lease rather than a permanent right.

---

## Purpose

Delegation without limits is abdication. This policy defines what "AI may assist" means in enforceable terms, so that a process owner granting an L3 delegation is doing so within a known envelope, and an auditor can reconstruct what was permitted at any point in time.

## Statement

No AI agent shall act with a delegation level exceeding the ceiling declared for the process, nor exceeding the ceiling for the data classification it is acting upon. Restricted-classification data shall never be processed autonomously, irrespective of any delegation granted. A delegation shall be granted only where the process declares an explicit decision space, escalation trigger and evidence requirement, and shall lapse if unreviewed at the end of its review cadence.

## Rules

- L0 and L1 may be granted by any process owner within the framework.
- L2 requires a published decision space and an escalation trigger, and approval by the Delegation Review Board chair.
- L3 requires approval by the full Delegation Review Board, a hard numeric threshold, and a named human reviewer.
- L4 requires full Board approval, a closed candidate set, mandatory decision rationale, and monthly audit sampling.
- Any delegation may be suspended immediately by the chair, the CISO or the Finance Controller.
- A delegation without a reviewer and a review cadence is downgraded automatically to L2.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_1.1`
- - `Proc_1.4`
- - `Proc_3.1`
- - `Proc_3.2`
- - `Proc_4.1`
- - `Proc_4.2`
- - `Proc_5.1`
- - `Proc_5.2`
- - `Proc_5.4`
- - `Proc_6.1`
- - `Proc_6.3`

## Enforcement

```yaml
mode: pre_action
enforced_by:
  - pfc-validator
  - mcp-gateway
  - delegation-review-board
on_violation: block
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: null
```

## Rationale

Autonomous agents are most valuable exactly where they are least supervised — high volume, low value, rule-bound decisions. Capping delegation at those points, and making every grant reviewable, converts AI from an unbounded risk into a managed capability.

## Exceptions

_No exceptions are granted under this policy._

# Catalogue and Contract First

> **policy_catalog_first** · sourcing policy · version 1.0.0

Requires that existing catalogue items and contracted supply are exhausted before new sourcing is initiated, and that any departure from them is measured and justified.

---

## Purpose

Contract leakage — buying what is already under contract at a higher price — is the single largest source of value erosion in a mature procurement function. Catalogue-first makes the default path the cheapest path.

## Statement

Every purchase requirement shall be matched against approved catalogue items and active contracts before being routed to a sourcing event. Where a requirement cannot be met from existing supply, the departure shall be recorded with its value consequence and reviewed as part of contract coverage reporting.

## Rules

- Matching is performed at intake and re-performed before purchase order issue.
- A catalogue order above the delegated value threshold requires human confirmation of the match.
- Payment shall be blocked for spend without a compliant requisition, except where a documented non-PO basis exists.
- Contract coverage rate is reported monthly by category.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_2.1`
- - `Proc_4.1`
- - `Proc_4.2`

```yaml
mode: pre_action
enforced_by:
  - pfc-validator
  - mcp-gateway
  - coupa-block
on_violation: block
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: Category Manager
```

## Rationale

Coverage is only a target if it is enforced at the moment of ordering. Blocking at intake and at PO issue makes the rule structural rather than advisory.

# Competitive Tendering

> **policy_competitive_tendering** · sourcing policy · version 1.0.0

Requires competition for material spend, sets the pre-commissioning discipline that makes an award defensible, and defines the circumstances in which a single source is permitted.

---

## Purpose

Competition is the mechanism that converts supplier willingness to pay into captured value. But competition without discipline is theatre: criteria drifting after bids arrive, or a shortlist that was never really open. This policy governs both the requirement to compete and the pre-commissioning discipline.

## Statement

Spend above the competitive threshold shall be awarded through a competitive process with a minimum of three invited suppliers, unless a single source is justified and approved at award level. Evaluation criteria, weighting and the supplier shortlist shall be approved and locked before the event is published. Any change to locked criteria after publication voids the event.

## Rules

- The competitive threshold is defined by category and reviewed annually.
- Requirements, evaluation criteria, weighting and shortlist are approved before publication.
- Locked criteria are stored with a cryptographic hash; divergence is detectable.
- A single-source award requires a written justification from one of: sole-source capability, intellectual property, regulatory constraint, or documented market failure.
- Clarifications are issued to all participants, never to one.
- A single-bid outcome requires justification at award level and is reported.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_3.1`

```yaml
  - ariba-event-guard

override_authority: Delegated Approver
```

## Rationale

The lock is the point. An award defended on criteria that were decided after the bids are visible is not defensible, and it teaches suppliers that the process is negotiable.

# Contract Management

> **policy_contract_management** · compliance policy · version 1.0.0

Requires that contracts be executed from approved templates, that deviations from the template be reviewed, and that obligations inside executed contracts be tracked rather than assumed.

---

## Purpose

A contract without an obligation register is a document, not a control. This policy makes the executed contract a live object with tracked obligations, and it prevents bespoke paper from quietly replacing the standards that protect the organisation.

## Statement

Contracts shall be executed from approved templates. Any deviation from a template clause shall be recorded in the deviation register and reviewed by Legal. On execution, the contract's obligations — dates, notice periods, escalators, service levels and renewal terms — shall be extracted into a tracked obligation register.

## Rules

- Only approved templates may be used for contracts above the low-value threshold.
- Deviations from standard clauses require Legal review and are recorded with the rationale.
- Obligation extraction is mandatory and must complete within 24 hours of execution.
- Renewal and notice dates generate automated reminders at 180, 120 and 60 days.
- Commercial terms may not be varied away from the award without a recorded approval.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_3.3`
- - `Proc_3.5`
- - `Proc_4.1`
- - `Proc_4.2`
- - `Proc_1.6`
- - `Proc_6.4`

```yaml
mode: pre_action
enforced_by:
  - pfc-validator
  - mcp-gateway
  - clm-guard
on_violation: escalate
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: Legal Counsel
```

## Rationale

Terms negotiated but unenforced, and obligations known but untracked, are the two ways a well-negotiated contract still fails. Automation of obligation capture is the highest-leverage intervention available.

# Data Classification and AI Handling

> **policy_data_classification** · security policy · version 1.0.0

Classifies procurement data, caps what an AI agent may process at each level, and requires that agent access to the framework itself be governed and logged.

---

## Purpose

Delegation is meaningless without a data ceiling. A process that grants an L3 delegation is only safe if the data it acts upon is appropriately classified — and some data may never be processed autonomously at all.

## Statement

Procurement data shall be classified as public, internal, confidential or restricted. An AI agent shall not process data classified above the ceiling declared for the step it is acting in. Data classified as restricted shall never be processed by an agent acting autonomously, irrespective of any delegation granted. - Every process input, output and step declares a data classification.

- All agent queries to the framework are logged and available for audit.

# Fraud and Duplicate Control

> **policy_fraud_and_duplicate_control** · compliance policy · version 1.0.0

Sets the controls that protect against payment redirection, duplicate payment and false invoicing, including the independent verification requirement for supplier banking data.

---

## Purpose

Payment fraud is cheap to commit and expensive to detect after settlement. The controls that stop it are unglamorous: independent verification, duplicate detection, combination screening and a release that requires two people.

## Statement

Changes to supplier banking data shall be verified through a channel independent of the request. Payment release shall require dual control. Invoices shall be screened for duplication, and a screening hold shall only be cleared by a named human. Combination signals — a recent bank change together with an unusual invoice — shall be treated as a hold trigger regardless of individual severity.

## Rules

- Bank-detail changes are verified by callback to a previously held contact number, never to a number on the change request.
- Payment release requires dual authorisation; an agent may never release a payment.
- Duplicate screening uses probabilistic matching; a hold is cleared only by a human with a recorded reason.
- Payment recalls are blocked at the supplier level pending fraud investigation.
- Hold volumes, release reasons and overrides are audited monthly.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_5.1`
- - `Proc_5.2`
- - `Proc_5.3`
- - `Proc_5.4`
- - `Proc_6.1`

```yaml
  - treasury-dual-control
on_violation: block
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: Fraud & Compliance Analyst
```

## Rationale

The verification channel is the whole control. Every real payment-redirection fraud exploited a channel that was not independent of the request — a reply-all email, a number in the request, a known contact who was also the requester.

# Intake Quality

> **policy_intake_quality** · operational policy · version 1.0.0

Sets the completeness standard for purchase requests and the requirement that a request be specific enough to be sourced without further clarification.

---

## Purpose

Vague requests are the largest single driver of procurement cycle time. They cause back-and-forth, incomplete RFx packages, mis-scoped contracts and disputes. Quality at intake pays for itself many times over downstream.

## Statement

A purchase request shall state the business need, the specification, the quantity or volume, the required date, the cost centre and the budget holder. A request that does not meet the completeness standard shall be returned to the requester with the specific missing fields identified, and shall not be progressed by procurement staff on the requester's behalf.

## Rules

- The completeness standard is defined per category and published.
- A request must be able to be sourced without asking the requester a further question about specification, volume or date.
- Return-for-correction is a designed outcome, not a failure, and is measured as such.
- The share of requests requiring clarification at the sourcing stage is a supplier-quality indicator of intake quality.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_2.1`
- - `Proc_2.2`
- - `Proc_4.1`

## Enforcement


# Master Data Quality

> **policy_master_data_quality** · operational policy · version 1.0.0

Sets the quality standard for supplier, material and catalogue master data, and requires that incomplete or duplicated records be remediated rather than tolerated.

---

## Purpose

Automation is only as good as the data it operates on. An agent reasoning over a supplier record with a stale tax identifier is not wrong in an obvious way — it is confidently wrong, which is worse. Master data quality is therefore a control, not housekeeping.

## Statement

All master data records shall be complete, unique, current and attributable. A record failing a mandatory data-quality rule shall not be used in an automated transaction until remediated. Records shall carry provenance for every field that originates outside the organisation.

## Rules

- Mandatory completeness, uniqueness, validity and currency rules are published per object type.
- A record failing a blocking rule may not be used in an automated transaction.
- Externally sourced fields record their provenance and retrieval date.
- Data quality is measured continuously and reported by owner.
- Remediation is prioritised by the business impact of the records affected, not by record count.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_3.4`
- - `Proc_3.5`
- - `Proc_6.1`
- - `Proc_6.3`

## Enforcement

```yaml
mode: pre_action
enforced_by:
  - pfc-validator
  - master-data-guard
on_violation: block
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: Supplier Master Data Owner
```

## Rationale

Blocking on quality is uncomfortable and correct. A record that is 92% complete is not 92% as useful as a complete record; in automated transactions it is a source of silent error.

## Exceptions

_No exceptions are granted under this policy._

# Material Master Governance

> **policy_material_master_governance** · operational policy · version 1.0.0

Defines ownership of material master data, the boundary between procurement and supply chain, and the standard against which material records are complete and unique.

---

## Purpose

The boundary between what is bought and what is received is where physical procurement processes fail. This policy makes ownership explicit — procurement owns the data, supply chain owns the custody — so that neither side can assume the other has closed the loop.

## Statement

Procurement owns the creation, enrichment and quality of material master records. Supply Chain owns physical custody, warehouse receipt and inventory posting. The receipt path for each material shall be declared on the material record and shall be unambiguous as to who confirms quantity and who owns variance. Material records shall be unique, and a creation that matches an existing material within tolerance shall be blocked for steward review.

## Rules

- Material records must be complete against the published required-field standard.
- A duplicate search precedes every creation.
- The receipt path is mandatory on the material record before any purchase order is raised against it.
- Material master changes are impact-analysed against open transactions before being applied.
- Procurement shall not post inventory quantities; Supply Chain shall not create material master records.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_3.4`
- - `Proc_4.3`

## Enforcement

```yaml
mode: pre_action
enforced_by:
  - pfc-validator
  - erp-master-data-guard
on_violation: block
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: Procurement Operations Lead
```

## Rationale

Duplicated materials fragment spend and destroy leverage; ambiguous quantity ownership creates stock that nobody owns. Both are cheap to prevent at creation and expensive to fix later.

## Exceptions

_No exceptions are granted under this policy._

# Procurement Policy of Record

> **policy_procurement_policy_of_record** · operational policy · version 1.0.0

The single authoritative statement of how procurement is to be run in this organisation: the obligations that hold across every category, the framework itself as the policy artefact, and the requirement that practice follows the published process.

---

## Purpose

Procurement policy is usually scattered across a policy portal, category playbooks, buyer habits and unwritten rules. This policy establishes one location, and makes the process framework — versioned in Git and published through the management system — the authoritative description of how procurement is performed.

## Statement

All procurement activity shall be performed in accordance with the published process objects in the Procurement Process Framework. Where practice diverges from a published process, the divergence shall be either corrected or the process shall be amended through the co-design process. No process shall be executed by an AI agent that is not published in the framework with an active status and an explicit delegation declaration.

## Rules

- The framework repository is the single source of truth; the management system is its published view, not a second copy.
- Every process has a named owner and a review date. An overdue review is automatically flagged and the process is not served to agents at L2 or above.
- Local deviations are permitted only as recorded exceptions with an owner and an expiry date.
- Practitioner contributions are made as pull requests and reviewed by at least one domain peer and the process owner.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_1.1`
- - `Proc_1.2`
- - `Proc_1.3`
- - `Proc_1.4`

```yaml
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: Procurement Governance
```

## Rationale

A process framework that is not the operating standard is documentation. Making the published framework authoritative removes the gap between what is written and what is done, and gives AI agents a single, versioned thing to obey.
