# Segregation of Duties

> **policy_segregation_of_duties** · compliance policy · version 1.0.0

Prohibits any single person or agent from preparing, approving and executing the same transaction, and defines the compensating controls where separation is not practicable.

---

## Purpose

Most procurement fraud is not sophisticated; it is one person able to do three things in sequence. Segregation of duties is the oldest control in the discipline and the one most often lost as organisations automate.

## Statement

No individual or AI agent shall both prepare a transaction and approve it, and no individual or agent shall approve a transaction they prepared. Where separation is not practicable due to scale or role design, a compensating control shall be documented and reviewed by the Delegation Review Board.

## Rules

- The preparer of a requisition, purchase order, invoice or award may not be its approver.
- An AI agent acting as preparer may never act as approver of the same record.
- Segregation checks are enforced at routing time and are logged.
- Breaches are reported to the Delegation Review Board within one business day.

# Supplier Onboarding and Due Diligence

> **policy_supplier_onboarding** · supplier policy · version 1.0.0

Requires due diligence, sanctions screening and independent banking verification before a supplier may transact, and prohibits any activation that bypasses it.

---

## Purpose

Onboarding is the gate through which every future transaction with a supplier passes. An incomplete gate means the organisation is transacting with someone it has not verified — and it will keep doing so indefinitely.

title: Thresholds and Approvals
text: Thresholds and Approvals policy thresholds and approvals · financial policy · version 1.0.0 Defines the approval matrix — who approves what, at what value, and under which delegation — and the aggregation rule that prevents value being split to evade it. --- Purpose Approval matrices fail in two ways: they are ambiguous about who may approve what, or they are evaded by splitting. This policy addresses both, and it is the reference against which every AI delegation threshold in the framework is expressed. Statement No commitment of spend shall be made without approval by the role designated for that value band. Approval requirements shall be computed on an aggregated value across related requisitions within a rolling window, so that a commitment may not be reduced below a threshold by subdivision. # Thresholds and Approvals

> **policy_thresholds_and_approvals** · financial policy · version 1.0.0

Defines the approval matrix — who approves what, at what value, and under which delegation — and the aggregation rule that prevents value being split to evade it.

---

## Purpose

Approval matrices fail in two ways: they are ambiguous about who may approve what, or they are evaded by splitting. This policy addresses both, and it is the reference against which every AI delegation threshold in the framework is expressed.

## Statement

No commitment of spend shall be made without approval by the role designated for that value band. Approval requirements shall be computed on an aggregated value across related requisitions within a rolling window, so that a commitment may not be reduced below a threshold by subdivision. Delegated approval limits shall be recorded, time-bound and revocable.

## Rules

- Thresholds are expressed in the currency of record and reviewed annually.
- Related requisitions are aggregated by requester, supplier, category and time window before threshold evaluation.
- A delegated approver may not approve a request they prepared.
- An expedited approval outside the matrix requires a documented reason and retrospective review.

## Applies to

- - `Proc_2.1`
- - `Proc_3.2`
- - `Proc_4.1`
- - `Proc_4.2`
- - `Proc_5.2`
- - `Proc_5.4`

## Enforcement

```yaml
mode: pre_action
enforced_by:
  - pfc-validator
  - mcp-gateway
  - approval-engine
on_violation: block
ai_may_override: false
override_authority: Delegation Review Board
```

## Rationale

A threshold that can be evaded by subdivision is a suggestion. Aggregation converts a nominal control into a real one, and it is precisely the control that bounds autonomous agent behaviour.

## Exceptions

_No exceptions are granted under this policy._

## Compliance evidence

- approval_matrix_version
- aggregation_log
- expedited_approvals

## Related

_None._

# Align Global Strategy

> **Proc_1.1** · Procurement > Strategy and Performance > Align Global Strategy

Translates enterprise objectives into a procurement strategy: the value procurement will create, the categories in scope, the spend under management and the levers available to deliver it.

---

## Purpose

Procurement cannot execute a strategy it does not own. This process establishes the enterprise procurement strategy as a first-class business artefact, aligned to enterprise goals, and published so that every downstream process — intake, sourcing, contract — can be evaluated against it.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Enterprise objectives and financial plan

- Savings and risk ambition

**Out of scope**

## Trigger

- Material change in portfolio or organisation

## Preconditions

# Manage Risk

> **Proc_1.3** · Procurement > Strategy and Performance > Manage Risk

Maintains the procurement risk register: identification, assessment, mitigation and escalation of third-party, concentration, continuity, compliance and ESG risks across the supplier portfolio.

---

## Purpose

Procurement is the function most exposed to third-party risk, and the one that sees it first. This process turns scattered risk observations into an owned, scored, funded mitigation plan, and ensures that no risk is silently carried because nobody owned it.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Third-party and supplier risk
- Concentration and single-source risk
- Business continuity and resilience risk
- Compliance and sanctions exposure
- ESG and reputational risk
- Contractual risk positions

**Out of scope**

- Operational incident management
- Enterprise-wide enterprise risk register
- Supplier corrective action execution

## Trigger

- New supplier introduced
- Material change in spend or supply
- Incident or near-miss
- Quarterly risk review
- Regulatory change

## Preconditions

- Supplier master available
- Spend cube available

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Category Director | A | R |  |  | no |
| Risk & Compliance Manager | A | R | C |  | no |
| Category Manager |  | R |  |  | yes |
| Legal Counsel |  |  | C |  | no |
| CISO |  |  | C | I | no |
| Head of Procurement |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Supplier risk data (financial, compliance, ESG) | Dataset | Third-party risk providers | yes | confidential |
| Spend concentration by supplier | Dataset | SpendIQ | yes | confidential |
| Incidents and near misses | Dataset | Incident management | no | internal |

## Outputs

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Mitigation plans with owners | Dataset | Supplier action plans | yes | internal |

# Manage Procurement Improvements

> **Proc_1.4** · Procurement > Strategy and Performance > Manage Procurement Improvements

Turns operational evidence — cycle times, exception rates, leakage, agent performance — into a prioritised backlog of improvements to the process framework itself, and into published framework releases.

---

## Purpose

A process framework that never improves becomes a museum. This process is the framework's own feedback loop: it measures how the published processes actually perform, identifies where they create friction or risk, and drives the changes back into the repository as versioned improvements.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Process performance telemetry
- Exception and leakage analysis
- Benchmarking against industry performance
- Agent decision quality review
- Framework change proposals and releases

**Out of scope**

- Day-to-day operational troubleshooting
- System configuration changes
- Individual process execution

## Trigger

- Quarterly framework review cycle
- Performance KPI misses its target

- Agent audit shows a decision-quality issue

## Preconditions

- Process telemetry available
- Framework version published

## Roles

# Manage Savings Funnel

> **Proc_1.5** · Procurement > Strategy and Performance > Manage Savings Funnel

Defines, validates, tracks and reports the savings funnel — from identified opportunity through to finance-validated realised savings — and detects leakage at every stage.

---

## Purpose

Savings are the most over-claimed number in procurement. This process makes savings auditable by insisting on a finance-validated baseline, a documented validation at each stage, and explicit visibility of value lost between stages.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Savings definition and methodology
- Pipeline stage definitions and entry criteria
- Validation with finance
- Realisation tracking
- Leakage analysis

**Out of scope**

- Negotiation execution
- Budget ownership
- Financial reporting outside procurement

## Trigger

- Savings opportunity identified
- Negotiation outcome recorded
- Contract price change
- Category strategy savings plan published

## Preconditions

- Finance-validated baseline available for the category

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Category Manager | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Category Director | A |  |  | I | no |
| Finance Business Partner | A | R | C |  | no |
| Procurement Operations Lead |  |  | C | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

# Manage Re-Negotiations

> **Proc_1.6** · Procurement > Strategy and Performance > Manage Re-Negotiations

Runs the re-negotiation cycle: build the renewal calendar, benchmark current pricing, prepare and execute the re-negotiation, and capture the price-down back into contracts and catalogue pricing.

---

## Purpose

Contracts are signed once and paid for years. Re-negotiation is the mechanism that returns value at renewal without a sourcing event, and it must be systematic — driven by a calendar and benchmarks, not by a buyer noticing a price.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Renewal calendar and notice periods
- Price benchmarking
- Re-negotiation preparation and execution
- Price-down capture into contracts and catalogues
- Escalation to a full re-sourcing event

**Out of scope**

- New sourcing events (Proc_3.1)
- Supplier performance management
- Payment and invoice processing

## Trigger

- Contract notice window approaches
- Market price movement detected
- Volume or scope change
- Supplier performance deterioration

## Preconditions

- Contract with a known renewal and notice date
- Current spend and price history available

# Govern Sustainability and ESG

> **Proc_1.7** · Procurement > Strategy and Performance > Govern Sustainability and ESG

Sets and enforces sustainability and ESG expectations across the supplier base: targets, supplier data collection, assessment, green sourcing levers, claims verification and disclosure.

---

## Purpose

Procurement holds the largest controllable lever on an organisation's environmental and social footprint — roughly two thirds of it sits in the supply base. This process makes that lever deliberate and evidenced rather than aspirational.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Scope 3 targets and their translation into supplier expectations
- Supplier ESG data collection and assessment
- Sustainability criteria in sourcing and contracting
- Verification of supplier claims
- ESG reporting and disclosure support

**Out of scope**

- Operational emissions measurement
- Public sustainability reporting ownership
- Product-level environmental compliance

## Trigger

- New supplier onboarding
- Sourcing event in an ESG-sensitive category
- External disclosure cycle
- Regulatory requirement change

# Request to Buying Channel

> **Proc_2.1** · Procurement > Intake Management > Request to Buying Channel

Captures a purchase requirement, qualifies it against strategy, budget and thresholds, matches it to existing catalogue and contract supply, and routes it to the correct buying channel — or rejects it with a reason.

---

## Purpose

This is the gateway that keeps the rest of procurement clean. Its job is to resolve, as early as possible, the three questions that cause most downstream waste: can we buy this from what we already have, can we afford it, and does it need a full sourcing event or not.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Purchase requirement capture from any function

- Budget and threshold qualification
- Routing to catalogue, sourcing or rejection
- Requester feedback and transparency

**Out of scope**

- Requisition approval (Proc_4.1)

# Demand Management

> **Proc_2.2** · Procurement > Intake Management > Demand Management

Consolidates, de-duplicates, analyses and shapes demand across the enterprise so that sourcing runs against a clear, aggregated picture rather than a stream of isolated requests.

---

## Purpose

Demand arrives fragmented and duplicated. Aggregating it before sourcing is what creates competitive tension — a category with 40 separate small requests has no leverage; the same demand expressed as one aggregated event does. This process is where that leverage is built.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Demand aggregation across functions
- Duplication detection
- Demand pattern analysis and forecasting
- Demand shaping — pre-sourcing engagement, standardisation
- Published demand plan for sourcing

**Out of scope**

- Sourcing event execution
- Budget allocation
- Supplier capacity commitments

## Trigger

- Intake volume reaches a consolidation threshold
- Planning cycle opens
- Duplicate pattern detected
- Supplier capacity constraint

## Preconditions

- Proc_2.1 producing classified requests
- Category strategy published

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Category Manager | A | R |  |  | no |
| Procurement Business Partner |  | R |  |  | yes |
| Demand Planner |  | R | C |  | no |
| Requester |  |  | C | I | no |
| Category Director |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qualified and classified requests | Dataset | Proc_2.1 | yes | internal |
| Historical demand and spend | Dataset | SpendIQ | yes | internal |
| Supplier capacity and lead-time data | Dataset | SRM | no | confidential |

| Demand pattern analysis | Document | Category review | yes | internal |
| Duplication and fragmentation report | Report | Proc_1.4 | yes | internal |

# Sourcing

> **Proc_3.1** · Procurement > Source to Contract > Sourcing

Turns a qualified requirement into a published, competitive sourcing event: requirement analysis, market analysis, sourcing strategy, approved shortlist, RFx authoring, review and publication.

---

## Purpose

Sourcing is where value and risk are actually created or destroyed. Its design principle is *pre-commission*: the strategy, the event type, the shortlist and the evaluation criteria are all decided and approved **before** suppliers see anything, so that the outcome is defensible by construction rather than by argument afterwards.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Requirement analysis
- Supplier market analysis
- Sourcing strategy and event type selection
- Supplier shortlisting and due diligence
- RFx authoring, review and publication
- Event management — clarifications and addenda

**Out of scope**

- Bid evaluation (Proc_3.2)
- Contract drafting (Proc_3.3)
- Category strategy definition

## Trigger

- Consolidated demand plan published
- Contract renewal approaching with re-sourcing decision
- Compliance-driven market engagement
- Strategic sourcing lever scheduled

## Preconditions

- Approved sourcing strategy from Proc_1.2
- Budget confirmed for the event
- Requisition or demand approved

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Procurement Business Partner | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Category Manager |  |  | C | I | no |
| Legal Counsel |  |  | C |  | no |
| Finance Business Partner |  |  | C |  | no |

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Time to publish | Working days from approved strategy to published event | < 10 days |
| Competitive participation | Share of published events receiving more than one bid | > 85% |
| Shortlist quality | Share of shortlisted suppliers that respond with a valid bid | > 70% |

## Risks and controls

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Criteria are changed after bids are received, voiding the process | Criteria are hashed and locked at publication; any change voids the event and forces re-issue |
| The shortlist is too narrow, producing a single bid | Shortlist approval requires a minimum viable competitive set; single-bid outcomes trigger a mandatory justification at award |
| Confidential information leaks through clarifications | Clarifications are checked against the confidentiality classification before issue |

## Exceptions and escalation

- - **Fewer than three qualified suppliers exist in the market** → Escalate to the Category Director for a documented market-failure justification and a single-source path, or a decision not to proceed.
- - **A requirement changes materially after publication** → Void the event, notify all participants, revise and re-publish. Do not continue with the original event.

# Awarding

> **Proc_3.2** · Procurement > Source to Contract > Awarding

Evaluates bids against the pre-declared criteria, produces a traceable award recommendation, obtains the approvals required by policy, notifies bidders and records the award into the savings funnel.

---

## Purpose

Awarding is where a sourcing event either produces a defensible decision or produces a dispute. Its design principle is *traceability*: every score, every comment and every decision must be reconstructable months later by someone who was not in the room.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Bid receipt and compliance screening
- Evaluation against locked criteria
- Clarification and negotiation rounds
- Award recommendation
- Approval and award notification
- Award recording into the savings funnel

**Out of scope**

- Contract drafting and negotiation (Proc_3.3)
- Sourcing event creation
- Supplier performance scoring

## Trigger

- Sourcing event closes
- Clarification round requested
- Evaluation scorecard complete

## Preconditions

- Published sourcing event
- Locked evaluation criteria
- Bid confidentiality maintained

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Procurement Business Partner | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Evaluator |  | R | C |  | yes |
| Category Manager | A |  | C |  | no |
| Delegated Approver | A |  |  | I | no |
| Legal Counsel |  |  | C |  | no |
| Supplier |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Received bids | Dataset | Ariba Sourcing | yes | confidential |
| Locked evaluation criteria | Dataset | Proc_3.1 | yes | confidential |
| Weighting and scoring model | Document | Category strategy | yes | internal |

## Outputs

| Completed evaluation scorecard | Dataset | Event record | yes | confidential |
| Approved award recommendation | Document | Event record | yes | confidential |

| Validated savings entry | Record | Proc_1.5 | yes | internal |

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Time to award | Working days from event close to award approval | < 10 days |
| Evaluation coverage | Share of bids scored against every locked criterion | 100% |
| Award justification completeness | Share of award records with complete rationale and approvals | 100% |

## Risks and controls

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Award rationale cannot be reconstructed later | Scorecard, evidence, clarifications and rationale are immutable records attached to the event |
| Pressure to award to a preferred supplier outside the process | Closed candidate set and hard validation prevent an unapproved supplier entering the award |
| Bid confidentiality breached by an agent summarising competitor data | Cross-bid data isolation is enforced in the agent context assembly, not merely instructed |

## Exceptions and escalation

- - **Only one compliant bid received** → Require a documented single-bid justification approved at award level before proceeding, and record it against the event.
- - **No bid meets the mandatory requirements** → Do not award. Either re-issue the event with the requirement clarified, or cancel with a documented business decision.

- evaluation_scorecard
- award_decision_record
- approval_chain
- decision_rationale
- notification_log

# Contracting

> **Proc_3.3** · Procurement > Source to Contract > Contracting

Converts an approved award into an executed, compliant contract: template selection, drafting from award terms, legal and commercial review, negotiation, signature, activation and obligation tracking.

---

## Purpose

An award is a decision; a contract is an obligation. This process ensures the contract reflects the award exactly, that deviations from the template are deliberate and reviewed, and that once signed the obligations inside it are tracked rather than forgotten.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Contract type and template selection
- Drafting from award terms
- Legal and commercial review
- Supplier negotiation
- Signature and activation
- Obligation and milestone register

**Out of scope**

- Term enrichment to transactional systems (Proc_3.5)
- Supplier performance management
- Payment execution

## Trigger

- Award approved
- Contract renewal
- Amendment required
- Framework agreement addition

## Preconditions

- Award decision recorded
- Approved contract template available

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Procurement Business Partner | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Legal Counsel | A | R | C |  | no |
| Category Manager |  |  | C | I | no |
| Finance Business Partner |  |  | C |  | no |
| Supplier |  |  | C | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Award decision record | Record | Proc_3.2 | yes | confidential |
| Award terms and commercial schedule | Dataset | Proc_3.1 / 3.2 | yes | confidential |
| Approved contract templates | Document | framework/templates | yes | internal |
| Standard terms and playbook | Document | Legal | no | internal |

## Outputs

| Name | Type | Destination | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Executed contract | Document | CLM | yes | confidential |
| Deviation register (from template) | Dataset | CLM | yes | confidential |
| Obligation and milestone register | Dataset | CLM | yes | internal |

## Steps

_Each step declares its own AI delegation. The effective level is the minimum of the step level and the process default (see [AI Delegation Matrix](../../governance/AI-Delegation-Matrix.md))._

### Step 1 · Select the contract type and template

  level: L1
  authority: recommend
  data_classification: confidential

      - policy_approved_contract_templates
    thresholds: {}

  constraints: []
  guardrails: []

  human_checkpoint: required
  reversible: true

### Step 2 · Draft the contract from the template and award terms

# Govern Inventory and Material Master

> **Proc_3.4** · Procurement > Source to Contract > Govern Inventory and Material Master

Owns the procurement side of physical material data: creating and enriching material master records, guaranteeing their quality and uniqueness, and declaring the boundary with supply chain for physical receipt.

---

## Purpose

Physical goods fail at the seam between procurement and supply chain. Procurement owns the *data* about what is bought; supply chain owns the *custody* of what arrives. This process makes that boundary explicit, guarantees that the data on which all matching depends is correct, and prevents the duplicate materials that quietly inflate spend and break category analysis.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Material master creation and enrichment
- Classification, unit-of-measure and tax attributes
- Data completeness and duplicate detection
- Receipt-path declaration with supply chain
- Material master change governance

**Out of scope**

- Warehouse execution and physical inventory counting
- Purchase order creation
- Supplier master data

## Trigger

- New material purchased for the first time
- Material master change requested
- Duplicate or incomplete record detected
- Receipt variance reported

## Preconditions

- Material requirement identified in a requisition or contract
- Supply chain receipt boundary agreed for the category

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Procurement Operations Lead | A | R |  |  | no |
| Master Data Steward |  | R | C |  | yes |
| Supply Chain Lead |  |  | C | I | no |
| Category Manager |  |  | C |  | no |
| Finance Business Partner |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Declared receipt path | Record | Material master / process record | yes | internal |
| Duplicate and completeness exception list | Dataset | Master data queue | yes | internal |

## Steps

# Transaction Enablement

> **Proc_3.5** · Procurement > Source to Contract > Transaction Enablement

Extracts the commercial terms from an executed award or contract and enriches the transactional systems — catalogues, item records, supplier pricing, match validation rules — so that every downstream transaction happens on the right terms without human intervention.

---

## Purpose

Negotiated terms that never reach the transactional systems are worth nothing at the moment of ordering. This process is the automation backbone of the framework: it is what makes three-way matching, price validation and contract coverage checks work automatically instead of as manual detective work.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Term extraction from executed contracts and awards
- Mapping to catalogue, item and supplier records
- Generation of validation and matching rules
- Publication to ERP and P2P systems
- Reconciliation and completeness reporting

**Out of scope**

- Requisition and PO creation
- Invoice matching
- Contract authoring

## Trigger

- Contract executed
- Award recorded with a framework agreement
- Contract amended or price changed
- Catalogue price stale beyond tolerance

## Preconditions

- Executed contract or framework award available
- Target catalogue and item records identified

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |

| Contract Manager |  | R | C |  | no |
| Category Manager |  |  | C | I | no |
| Finance Business Partner |  |  | C | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

# Approve Purchase Requisition

> **Proc_4.1** · Procurement > Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order > Approve Purchase Requisition

Validates a qualified requisition for completeness, budget and contract coverage, routes it to the right approver according to the threshold matrix, and releases it for purchase order creation.

---

## Purpose

This is the point where a request becomes a commitment of money. Everything before it is reversible; everything after it is not. The process exists to make sure that four things are true before that line is crossed: the request is complete, the money exists, the price is contractually correct, and the right person has approved it.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Requisition completeness and correctness validation
- Budget availability verification
- Contract coverage check
- Split-request detection
- Approval routing and delegation handling
- Release for PO creation

**Out of scope**

- PO creation (Proc_4.2)
- Sourcing (Proc_3.1)
- Demand management (Proc_2.2)

## Trigger

- Requisition submitted and qualified at intake
- Budget or contract position changed
- Requisition returned for correction

## Preconditions

- Requisition qualified at Proc_2.1
- Budget period open
- Supplier active

## Roles

# Create and Distribute Purchase Order

> **Proc_4.2** · Procurement > Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order > Create and Distribute Purchase Order

Builds, validates, approves and issues the purchase order against an approved requisition, applying contract pricing and complete master data, then transmits the order to the supplier.

---

## Purpose

Every invoice dispute and every unmatched payment traces back to a purchase order that was wrong or incomplete at the moment of issue. This process makes PO first-time-right the design target, and it is the highest-volume, most rule-bound process in the framework — which makes it the strongest candidate for delegation at L3.

## Scope

**In scope**

- PO construction from the approved requisition
- Contract price and term application
- PO data validation against the master-data standard
- Threshold approval for high-value orders
- PO issue and transmission to supplier
- Supplier acknowledgement monitoring

**Out of scope**

- Goods receipt (Proc_4.3)
- Invoice matching (Proc_5.2)
- Supplier master creation

## Trigger

- Requisition approved and released
- PO amendment required
- Supplier asks for a PO re-issue

## Preconditions

- Requisition approved
- Supplier active and transactable
- Contract pricing available where required

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Buyer / Procurement Business Partner | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Delegated Approver | A |  |  | I | no |
| Category Manager |  |  | C | I | no |
| Supplier |  |  |  | I | no |
| Finance Business Partner |  |  | C |  | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Released requisition | Record | Proc_4.1 | yes | internal |
| Contract pricing and terms | Dataset | CLM / Coupa catalogue | yes | confidential |
| Supplier master record | Record | SRM | yes | confidential |
| Material and item master data | Dataset | ERP | yes | internal |

## Outputs

| Name | Type | Destination | Required | Classification |

| Issued purchase order | Record | ERP / Coupa | yes | confidential |
| Transmitted order and supplier acknowledgement | Event | Business Network | yes | confidential |
| PO audit record | Record | Procurement audit log | yes | internal |

## Steps

# Receive Materials and Services

> **Proc_4.3** · Procurement > Purchase Requisition to Purchase Order > Receive Materials and Services

Confirms the arrival and acceptance of purchased materials and services, records the receipt in the transactional system, resolves variances, and completes the purchase order so that invoices can be matched.

---

## Purpose

The receipt is the third leg of the three-way match and the moment where the organisation takes possession of what it bought. It is also where quantity ownership is most often ambiguous — and where a careless receipt creates both financial exposure and stock that nobody owns.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Receipt expectation and delivery scheduling
- Physical receipt and inspection
- Receipt recording in the transactional system
- Variance, damage and rejection handling
- Inventory posting coordination with supply chain
- Purchase order completion

**Out of scope**

- Invoice matching (Proc_5.2)
- Warehouse execution
- Supplier corrective action

## Trigger

- Supplier delivery notification
- Goods arrive at the dock or service is delivered
- Purchase order due date approaches

## Preconditions

- Purchase order issued
- Receipt path declared on the material record
- Receiver identified

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Receiver / Storekeeper | A | R |  |  | no |
| Supply Chain Lead |  |  | C | I | no |
| Quality Inspector |  | R | C |  | no |
| Buyer / Procurement Business Partner |  |  | C | I | no |
| Supplier |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Delivery advice and packing list | Document | Supplier | no | internal |

  prohibited:
    - post_a_receipt_without_a_delivery_confirmation
    - close_a_line_with_an_open_dispute

  register_id: DR-006

    quantity and condition come from the delivery, the price from the order. A wrong posting is
    corrected by a reversal with the same audit trail.
  granted_by: Delegation Review Board
  granted_on: 2026-01-15

  steps:
    - 3

```

_Ceiling: an agent may never exceed this process default, whatever any step requests. Restricted-classification data caps any agent at L1 regardless of delegation._

## KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Receipt accuracy | Share of receipts recorded with no subsequent quantity or value correction | > 98% |
| Receipt timeliness | Elapsed time from physical arrival to system receipt, in hours | < 24 hours |
| Three-way match readiness | Share of invoices matched on first submission | > 90% |

## Risks and controls

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Quantity overstated to release an urgent invoice | Receipt validity checks, periodic physical-to-system reconciliation, audit sampling of high-value receipts |
| Stock received but never recorded, creating unowned inventory | Receipt path declared per material; unreconciled receipts reported as a standing exception |
| Service deliveries confirmed without evidence of performance | Service receipts require an acceptance record tied to the contracted service level |

## Exceptions and escalation

- - **Goods arrive without a purchase order** → Record against the declared receipt path as a non-PO receipt, quarantine the goods and raise an exception to Proc_5.3 for commercial resolution.
- - **Supplier delivers more than ordered** → undefined

## Audit and evidence

- goods_receipt_record
- inspection_result
- variance_record

# Receive Invoice

> **Proc_5.1** · Procurement > Invoice to Pay > Receive Invoice

Captures supplier invoices from every channel, validates their structure, screens them for duplication, fraud and sanctions exposure, and routes them into the matching process.

---

## Purpose

An invoice enters the organisation through this process, and this is the last point at which it can be stopped cleanly. The objective is to make capture automatic and reliable, and to catch the handful of invoices that are not what they appear to be before they consume payment capacity.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Invoice capture via EDI, e-invoice, portal, email and OCR
- Structural and mandatory-field validation
- Duplicate detection
- Fraud, bank-change and sanctions screening
- Routing to matching

**Out of scope**

- Matching and approval (Proc_5.2)
- Exception handling (Proc_5.3)
- Supplier master creation

## Trigger

- Supplier submits an invoice
- Invoice arrives by email or post
- System-generated invoice from a recurring service

## Preconditions

- Supplier active in the system
- Purchase order or approved non-PO basis exists

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts Payable Clerk | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Accounts Payable Manager | A |  | C |  | no |
| Supplier |  |  |  | I | no |
| Fraud & Compliance Analyst |  |  | C | I | no |
| Procurement Business Partner |  |  | C |  | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Supplier invoice | Document | Supplier / channel | yes | confidential |
| Supplier master and bank data | Record | SRM | yes | confidential |
| Purchase order and receipt records | Dataset | ERP | no | confidential |

## Outputs

| Validated invoice record | Record | Coupa Invoicing | yes | confidential |
| Duplicate hold record | Record | Exception queue | no | confidential |
| Screening outcome | Record | Fraud screening log | yes | restricted |

## Steps

_Each step declares its own AI delegation. The effective level is the minimum of the step level and the process default (see [AI Delegation Matrix](../../governance/AI-Delegation-Matrix.md))._

### Step 1 · Capture the invoice from the source channel

guardrails:
  - policy_fraud_and_duplicate_control
  - policy_data_classification
escalation:
  trigger: null
  to: null
  sla_hours: null
human_checkpoint: on_exception
reversible: true
evidence:
  - screening_outcome
  - duplicate_check_result
  - capture_log
```

_Ceiling: an agent may never exceed this process default, whatever any step requests. Restricted-classification data caps any agent at L1 regardless of delegation._

## KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auto-capture rate | Share of invoices captured without manual keying | > 85% |
| Duplicate rate | Duplicate invoices caught before payment, per 1,000 invoices | < 2 |
| Invoice completeness | Share of invoices passing structural validation on first submission | > 92% |

## Risks and controls

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Payment redirection fraud via changed bank details | Combination screening on bank change plus invoice characteristics; independent verification channel before release |
| Legitimate invoices held and supplier relationships damaged | Hold time limits with service-level targets; suppliers informed promptly of the hold and its reason |
| Duplicate invoices paid twice | Probabilistic duplicate detection plus a standing duplicate hold list reviewed daily |

## Exceptions and escalation

- - **Invoice received against a non-PO basis** → Route to Proc_5.3 for commercial resolution. Do not create a PO retrospectively to make the match work.
- - **Invoice received for a blocked or inactive supplier** → Hold and notify the supplier master owner. Do not activate the supplier as part of invoice processing.

## Audit and evidence

- capture_log
- duplicate_check_result
- screening_outcome

# Match and Approve Invoice

> **Proc_5.2** · Procurement > Invoice to Pay > Match and Approve Invoice

Matches the invoice against the purchase order and the goods receipt, evaluates variances against defined tolerances, routes the invoice for approval, and releases it into the payment run.

---

## Purpose

Matching is the control that ensures the organisation pays only for what it ordered and received. Its design goal is that the overwhelming majority of invoices match automatically and never touch a human, while every invoice that does not match carries with it a complete explanation of why.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Three-way match — invoice against PO and receipt
- Variance evaluation against tolerances
- Service receipt and period-based validation
- Approval routing per threshold
- Release into the payment run

**Out of scope**

- Payment execution (Proc_5.4)
- Exception resolution (Proc_5.3)
- Contract price verification

## Trigger

- Invoice validated and routed
- Receipt recorded against an open PO
- Tolerance rule change published

## Preconditions

- Invoice validated (Proc_5.1)
- PO issued
- Receipt recorded for physical goods

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts Payable Clerk | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Accounts Payable Manager | A |  | C |  | no |
| Business Unit Approver | A |  |  | I | no |
| Procurement Business Partner |  |  | C |  | no |
| Goods Receiver |  |  | C |  | no |
| Supplier |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Validated invoice | Record | Proc_5.1 | yes | confidential |
| Purchase order lines | Dataset | ERP | yes | confidential |
| Goods receipt records | Dataset | ERP | yes | internal |
| Tolerance and matching rules | Dataset | Proc_3.5 | yes | internal |

## Outputs

| Name | Type | Destination | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Match result | Record | Coupa Invoicing | yes | confidential |
| Approved invoice | Record | Payment run | yes | confidential |
| Exception with reason | Record | Exception queue | no | internal |

## Steps

_Each step declares its own AI delegation. The effective level is the minimum of the step level and the process default (see [AI Delegation Matrix](../../governance/AI-Delegation-Matrix.md))._

# Resolve Invoice Issue

> **Proc_5.3** · Procurement > Invoice to Pay > Resolve Invoice Issue

Classifies invoice exceptions, assigns them to the right owner with the context to act, resolves them — by correcting, disputing, writing off or cancelling — and feeds the recurring root cause back into process improvement.

---

## Purpose

An exception is only a problem twice: once for the invoice, and once for the process that produced it. This process closes the invoice and captures the cause, so the same failure does not recur and the framework improves with volume.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Exception detection and classification
- Ownership assignment and context packaging
- Investigation and evidence gathering
- Resolution — correct, dispute, write off, cancel
- Re-processing after resolution
- Root-cause capture

**Out of scope**

- Payment execution (Proc_5.4)
- Process improvement (Proc_1.4)
- Supplier corrective action (Proc_6.4)

## Trigger

- Match exception raised
- Duplicate hold
- Fraud screening hold
- Supplier dispute received
- Missing receipt or PO

## Preconditions

# Pay Invoice

> **Proc_5.4** · Procurement > Invoice to Pay > Pay Invoice

Schedules approved invoices into payment runs, applies early-payment discounts and run optimisations, verifies supplier banking data independently, releases payment and sends remittance advice.

---

## Purpose

This is the last irreversible act in the procurement chain: money leaves the organisation. Everything upstream produces a decision; this produces a consequence. The process is designed so that the consequence is always preceded by an independent verification of the destination account.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Payment run scheduling and optimisation
- Early-payment discount capture
- Supplier bank verification
- Payment release
- Remittance advice
- Payment reconciliation and archiving

**Out of scope**

- Supplier onboarding
- Currency hedging execution
- Statutory reporting

## Trigger

- Invoice approved for payment
- Payment run scheduled
- Discount deadline approaching

## Preconditions

- Invoice approved for payment
- Supplier bank data verified and current
- No active payment hold on the supplier

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts Payable Clerk | A | R |  |  | yes |
| Treasury Analyst | A | R | C |  | no |
| Accounts Payable Manager | A |  | C |  | no |
| Supplier |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approved invoices | Dataset | Proc_5.2 / 5.3 | yes | confidential |
| Supplier banking details | Record | SRM | yes | restricted |
| Payment terms and discount schedule | Dataset | CLM | yes | internal |

## Outputs

| Name | Type | Destination | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Payment run | Record | Treasury / bank file | yes | restricted |
| Remittance advice | Document | Supplier | yes | internal |
| Payment confirmation and reconciliation record | Record | ERP | yes | restricted |

## Steps

_Each step declares its own AI delegation. The effective level is the minimum of the step level and the process default (see [AI Delegation Matrix](../../governance/AI-Delegation-Matrix.md))._

## KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On-time payment rate | Share of invoices paid within contractual payment terms | > 95% |
| Early-payment discount captured | Value of discounts captured divided by discounts available | > 80% |
| Payment error rate | Payment runs requiring recall or correction, per 1,000 payments | < 1 |

## Risks and controls

| Risk | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Payment redirection through manipulated bank data | Independent verification channel; dual control on release; restricted data classification on banking details |
| Agent releases payment at scale | human_checkpoint is permanently `always` for this process — the agent may never release a payment without a human release action |
| Early-payment discounts missed | Discount deadlines are read from contract terms and drive the run schedule; missed discounts are reported |

## Exceptions and escalation

- - **Bank verification cannot be completed** → Do not pay. Hold the payment, notify the supplier master owner and the AP Manager, and escalate to the fraud analyst.
- - **Payment recalled by the bank** → Block the supplier's future payments, notify fraud and compliance, and reconcile the funds before any further run.

# Qualify Supplier

> **Proc_6.2** · Procurement > Supplier Management > Qualify Supplier

Tests a supplier against the qualification criteria for its category — capability, capacity, quality, financial standing and compliance — and grants or withholds approval to transact and to be considered in sourcing.

---

## Purpose

Onboarding proves a supplier exists and is safe to transact with. Qualification proves they can actually do the work. Separating the two lets a supplier be onboarded quickly for a small purchase while a large contract waits for full qualification — and prevents an unqualified supplier from being shortlisted simply because they were fast to sign up.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Qualification criteria definition per category
- Capability, quality, capacity and financial assessment
- Evidence collection and audit
- Approval to transact decision
- Re-qualification scheduling

**Out of scope**

- Supplier onboarding (Proc_6.1)
- Sourcing event execution
- Commercial negotiation

## Trigger

- Supplier requests approval for a new category
- New contract awarded to a supplier
- Qualification lapses
- Performance failure raises the need to re-qualify

## Preconditions

- Supplier onboarded (Proc_6.1)
- Qualification criteria published for the category

## Roles

# Offboard Supplier

> **Proc_6.3** · Procurement > Supplier Management > Offboard Supplier

Detects the conditions that end a supplier relationship, blocks transactions, resolves open commitments, revokes access, handles data retention and archiving, and confirms the outcome.

---

## Purpose

Offboarding is the process most often skipped and the one with the largest residual risk. A supplier left active can still receive orders, still receive personal data, and still be paid. This process makes the end of a relationship an explicit, evidenced action rather than an absence.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Offboarding trigger detection
- Transactional blocking
- Open commitment resolution — orders, invoices, claims
- Access revocation and data handling
- Notification and record archiving
- Completion attestation

**Out of scope**

- Supplier performance management
- Re-negotiation of an existing contract
- Legal proceedings

## Trigger

- Contract ended or expired
- Supplier terminated for cause
- Performance failure below threshold
- Risk event or sanctions finding
- Duplicate or inactive record cleanup

## Preconditions

- Offboarding trigger identified

## Roles

| Role | Accountable | Responsible | Consulted | Informed | AI may act |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Supplier Master Data Owner | A | R |  |  | no |
| Master Data Steward |  | R |  |  | yes |
| Accounts Payable Manager |  | R | C |  | no |
| Procurement Business Partner |  |  | C |  | no |
| Data Protection Officer |  |  | C | I | no |
| Supplier |  |  |  | I | no |

_A = accountable, R = responsible, C = consulted, I = informed. "AI may act" states whether an agent may perform this role at the level declared in the step, subject to the delegation ceiling for the process._

## Inputs

| Name | Type | Source | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Offboarding trigger | Record | CLM / SRM / incident | yes | internal |
| Open commitments inventory | Dataset | ERP / Coupa | yes | confidential |
| Data and access inventory | Dataset | Identity and data governance | yes | restricted |

## Outputs

| Name | Type | Destination | Required | Classification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blocked supplier status | Event | SRM / ERP | yes | internal |
| Resolved open commitments | Record | Procurement | yes | confidential |
| Data and access disposition record | Record | Data governance | yes | restricted |
| Offboarding attestation | Record | Audit | yes | internal |

## Steps

_Each step declares its own AI delegation. The effective level is the minimum of the step level and the process default (see [AI Delegation Matrix](../../governance/AI-Delegation-Matrix.md))._

# Manage Supplier Performance

> **Proc_6.4** · Procurement > Supplier Management > Manage Supplier Performance

Measures supplier performance against contracted service levels and commercial outcomes, reviews it with the supplier, agrees development or corrective action, and feeds the results back into sourcing strategy and renewal decisions.

---

## Purpose

Performance management is what turns a supplier relationship from a transaction into a managed relationship — and what gives the organisation evidence at renewal time. Without it, every renewal conversation starts from scratch and every poor performance is discovered as a surprise.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Performance scorecard definition
- Measurement against contracted service levels
- Performance review with the supplier
- Development plans and corrective actions
- Escalation and sourcing strategy feedback

**Out of scope**

- Supplier qualification (Proc_6.2)
- Supplier offboarding (Proc_6.3)
- Payment of incentives and penalties

## Trigger

- Review cycle scheduled
- Service level breach recorded
- Contract milestone reached
- Renewal approaching
- Incident attributable to a supplier

## Preconditions

- Contract with defined service levels
- Measurement data available

| Business Unit Sponsor |  |  | C | I | no |

# Award Recommendation

> **skills_award_recommendation** · howto · version 1.0.0

How to write an award recommendation that an approver can act on in minutes, and that remains defensible months later.

---

## When to use this skill

After evaluation, when presenting the award for approval.

## Prerequisites

- Completed evaluation scorecard
- Consolidated scores

## Method

### 1. State the outcome

Name the supplier, the price, the term and the total cost of ownership — not the unit price alone.

### 2. Show the basis

Present the score against each locked criterion and the margin over the next bid.

### 3. Disclose the exceptions

List every requirement the winner did not meet perfectly, and why that was acceptable. Hiding this is how a recommendation fails at approval.

### 4. Give the alternative

State what the second choice would have delivered and at what cost, so the approver can judge the trade-off.

### 5. State the risk

Name the risk being carried by this award and who owns it.

## Outputs

- Approved award recommendation

## Quality bar

The recommendation answers: who, at what price, on what basis, against which criteria, with what exceptions, and what the alternative was. Anything it does not answer is missing.

## Anti-patterns

- A recommendation that needs a meeting to explain.
- Omitting the runner-up and the margin, which the approver will ask for anyway.
- Framing the decision in terms of the relationship rather than the criteria.

# Market Benchmarking

> **skills_benchmarking** · analysis · version 1.0.0

How to establish what a fair price is for a given requirement, using comparable data rather than assertion, and how to cite it so the finding survives challenge.

---

## When to use this skill

Before a negotiation, when validating a savings figure, and when setting an internal target for a category.

## Prerequisites

- A specific, comparable requirement definition
- Access to external benchmark data

## Method

### 1. Define the comparable

State precisely what is being compared — volume, specification, service level, term, geography, delivery model. Benchmarking without this is price-shopping.

### 2. Collect the comparables

Gather multiple independent data points. Record source, date and basis for each.

### 3. Normalise

Adjust for scope, scale, term and conditions so the figures are genuinely comparable.

### 4. Position

State where the current position sits relative to the comparables, and how confident that statement is.

### 5. Cite

Attach the source and date to every figure used downstream, so it can be re-verified rather than re-argued.

## Outputs

- Benchmark analysis with cited sources
- Price position statement

## Quality bar

Every benchmark figure cites a source, a date and the comparability basis. An uncited number is not a benchmark.

## Anti-patterns

- Comparing a premium requirement against a commodity benchmark.
- Citing a single data point as a market range.
- Using a benchmark that is older than the market movement it is used to explain.

# Bid Evaluation

> **skills_bid_evaluation** · judgement · version 1.0.0

How to evaluate bids against pre-declared criteria consistently, evidencing every score so the evaluation can be reconstructed later.

---

## When to use this skill

After an RFx closes.

## Prerequisites

- Published, locked evaluation criteria
- Approved evaluation panel
- Received bids

## Method

### 1. Screen for compliance first

Establish which bids meet the mandatory requirements. Only compliant bids are evaluated on quality.

### 2. Evaluate criterion by criterion

Complete one criterion across all bids before moving to the next. Comparing across bids within a criterion reduces anchoring.

### 3. Score with evidence

For each score, record the specific part of the bid that justifies it. Not a general impression — a reference.

### 4. Consolidate and surface divergence

Compare evaluator scores and highlight where they diverge most. That divergence points to ambiguity in the requirement.

### 5. Re-read the criteria

After scoring, re-read the locked criteria. If the criteria could not distinguish between bids, the event was designed poorly — say so.

## Outputs

- Completed evaluation scorecard
- Consolidated scores with divergence flagged

## Quality bar

Every score carries the evidence that produced it. An evaluator's score without evidence is an opinion and does not survive audit.

## Anti-patterns

- Reading one bid fully and the others quickly.
- Comparing bids against each other rather than against the criteria.
- Adjusting a score after seeing the consolidated result without recording it.

# Budget Validation

> **skills_budget_validation** · judgement · version 1.0.0

How to verify that a commitment can be funded — checking available balance, encumbrances, period, category and the consequences of committing against a reserved balance.

---

## When to use this skill

Before a requisition is approved or released, and before any autonomous order is issued.

## Prerequisites

- Budget position and encumbrance data
- Cost centre and category of the requirement

## Method

### 1. Identify the funding source

Determine the cost centre, category and budget line the commitment belongs to.

### 2. Read the available position

Take the ledger balance, subtract outstanding encumbrances and reservations.

### 3. Check the period and category

Confirm the budget period is open and the spend is permitted within the category's restrictions.

### 4. Check the concentration

Confirm the commitment does not breach a volume, supplier or category concentration limit.

### 5. Encumber and record

Encumber the amount with a reference to the requisition, so it cannot be spent twice.

## Outputs

- Budget check result
- Encumbrance

## Quality bar

The check reflects commitments already made, not only the unspent balance. A balance that ignores encumbrances is not a balance.

## Anti-patterns

- Checking the nominal balance without outstanding encumbrances.
- Allowing commitment against a reserved or ring-fenced budget.
- Allowing commitment outside the budget period.

# Catalogue Matching

> **skills_catalogue_match** · judgement · version 1.0.0

How to match a requirement against approved catalogue items and contracted supply, and to explain the match well enough for a requester to disagree with it.

---

## When to use this skill

At intake, and again before a purchase order is issued.

## Prerequisites

- Approved catalogue
- Contracted pricing data
- The requirement specification

## Method

### 1. Extract the requirement attributes

Identify the attributes that determine suitability — specification, size, capacity, service level, certification.

### 2. Retrieve candidates

Search the approved catalogue and contracted items for candidates matching those attributes.

### 3. Score and rank

Rank on suitability first, then on price and terms. Never rank on price alone.

### 4. Check price and terms

Confirm the catalogue price is at or below the current contracted price for the same requirement.

### 5. Explain

State the matched item, the matching attributes and the residual gap, so a requester can accept or reject it.

## Outputs

- Catalogue match result with explanation
- Reuse or new-source recommendation

## Quality bar

Every recommendation names the item, the matching attributes and the price basis. If the explanation is missing, the match is not usable.

## Anti-patterns

- Matching on the item description alone, ignoring specification attributes.
- Accepting a substitute that meets the description but not the requirement.
- Forcing a match because something in the catalogue is better than nothing.

How to turn portfolio analysis into a category strategy that a practitioner can actually execute: demand profile, sourcing levers, savings plan, risk profile and review calendar.

When creating or refreshing a category strategy, and when a sourcing event needs to be justified against a strategy.

Describe what is bought, by whom, how often, and what drives the volume. Demand drivers determine which levers are viable.

Map the supplier base, concentration, switching costs and the credible alternatives for each significant requirement.

- Draft category strategy

- Savings plan and review calendar

# Contract Clause Review

> **skills_clause_review** · checklist · version 1.0.0

How to review a contract against the organisation's standard positions, identify the deviations that matter, and escalate the ones that do.

---

## When to use this skill

During internal legal review, and when a supplier returns a marked-up template.

## Prerequisites

- Clause playbook
- Deviation register from the template

## Method

### 1. Diff against the template

Compare the received contract to the approved template and list every deviation. Automate the diff; do not read it.

### 2. Categorise by risk

Liability, indemnity, termination, payment terms, IP, data protection, exclusivity, price escalation, audit rights, service levels.

### 3. Assess the consequential ones

For each material deviation, state the realistic exposure in the context of this deal's value and duration.

### 4. Recommend

Accept, amend with proposed wording, or escalate to the Delegation Review Board with a business justification.

### 5. Record the precedent

Record any accepted deviation so it becomes visible to the next negotiation — accepted deviations are how playbooks erode.

## Outputs

- Reviewed contract
- Deviation assessment with recommendation

## Quality bar

Every deviation from the playbook is listed, categorised by risk, and given a recommendation of accept, amend or escalate. None are silently accepted.

## Anti-patterns

- Reading a marked-up contract linearly and reacting to the first surprising clause.
- Accepting a liability increase because the deal is urgent.
- Ignoring the data protection clauses because this is a low-data engagement.

# Contract Negotiation

> **skills_contract_negotiation** · playbook · version 1.0.0

How to prepare for, conduct and close a contract negotiation: the position, the fallback sequence, and the discipline of never conceding without a trade.

---

## When to use this skill

Before any contract discussion with a supplier.

## Prerequisites

- Approved template and clause playbook
- Benchmarked price position
- Defined walk-away position

## Method

### 1. Set the position and the walk-away

Define the target, the acceptable range and the point at which you stop. Agree both internally before the conversation.

### 2. Build the fallback sequence

Pre-agree which concession you make first, second and third, and what you get for each. Never improvise the sequence live.

### 3. Trade, never gift

Every concession is exchanged. A longer term for a lower price; a volume commitment for a service level; a payment term for a discount.

### 4. Watch the late clauses

The final exchange is where pressure is applied. Do not accept a late change without re-running the approval for the new position.

### 5. Capture the value

Record the price-down, the term improvement and the obligation gained, and feed them into the contract and the transactional systems.

## Outputs

- Negotiation plan with fallback sequence
- Executed amendment with captured value

## Quality bar

Every concession in the final position has a corresponding concession obtained, and is recorded with its value.

## Anti-patterns

- Conceding unilaterally to preserve goodwill that was never tested.
- Negotiating without knowing the benchmark.
- Accepting a term change in the final minutes to avoid an extension.

# Supplier ESG Assessment

> **skills_esg_assessment** · analysis · version 1.0.0

How to assess a supplier's sustainability performance with proportionate rigour, distinguishing what is self-declared from what is verified.

---

## When to use this skill

During onboarding, at annual refresh, and when ESG criteria are applied in a sourcing event.

- Published ESG methodology
- Materiality threshold agreed

### 1. Establish materiality

Define which environmental and social dimensions matter for this category and why.

### 2. Collect with provenance

Record source, date and self-declared or verified status for every data point.

### 3. Score separately

Score verified and self-declared data on separate scales and present both.

### 4. Set proportionate requirements

Scale the evidence requirement to the supplier's size and the category's materiality.

Verify the material claims at a defined rate and record the outcome honestly.

# Invoice Exception Resolution

> **skills_exception_resolution** · playbook · version 1.0.0

How to clear an invoice exception efficiently: classify it, package the context, resolve it, and fix the cause so it does not recur.

---

## When to use this skill

Whenever an invoice is held or fails to match.

## Prerequisites

- A classified exception
- Access to the invoice, PO, receipt and contract records

## Method

### 1. Classify before acting

Assign the reason code first. The code determines the owner, the route and the expected resolution time.

### 2. Package the context

Assemble the invoice, PO, receipt, contract clause, discrepancy and prior attempts into a single package for the owner.

### 3. Investigate the cause

Determine what actually went wrong — a wrong price, a missing receipt, a late delivery, a mis-keyed invoice, a data error.

### 4. Choose the resolution

Correct the record, dispute with the supplier, write off, or cancel. Consider recovery probability and cost of pursuit.

### 5. Fix the cause

Raise the cause into the improvement backlog with the volume it explains. Repeat exceptions are a process defect.

## Outputs

- Resolution decision
- Root-cause record

## Quality bar

Each exception is closed with a decision and a cause. The cause is recorded even when the resolution was simple — the repetition data is the point.

## Anti-patterns

- Clearing the exception without recording the cause.
- Returning the invoice to the supplier as the default resolution.
- Fixing the same recurring cause by handling the symptom again.

# Master Data Quality Management

> **skills_master_data_quality** · howto · version 1.0.0

How to keep master records complete, unique, current and attributable — and how to stop a bad record being used in an automated transaction.

---

## When to use this skill

Whenever master data is created, enriched, changed or consumed by an automated process.

## Prerequisites

- Published data quality rules
- A named data owner

## Method

### 1. Define the rules per object type

Completeness, uniqueness, validity, currency and attribution, published and versioned.

### 2. Enforce at the point of use

The blocking check runs where the record is consumed, not only where it was created.

### 3. Reuse before create

Search for an existing fit before creating. Duplicates are cheaper to prevent than to merge.

### 4. Prioritise remediation by impact

Fix the records that affect the most value, not the ones that are easiest to count.

### 5. Measure and publish

Score continuously, publish by owner, and treat a falling score as an operational risk.

## Outputs

- Quality scorecard
- Remediation queue
- Blocking events

## Quality bar

A record failing a blocking rule is not used in an automated transaction. The rule is enforced by the system, not by a person remembering it.

## Anti-patterns

- Treating completeness as a percentage target rather than a rule.
- Letting incomplete records flow because the transaction is urgent.
- Restating historical data without recording the taxonomy version.

# Supplier Offboarding

> **skills_offboarding** · checklist · version 1.0.0

How to end a supplier relationship safely: block first, then resolve exposure, then dispose of data, then attest.

---

## When to use this skill

Whenever a supplier relationship ends, for any reason.

## Prerequisites

- A confirmed offboarding trigger
- The open commitments and data inventories

## Method

### 1. Block transactable status immediately

The first step, and irreversible in the session. Exposure takes days to close; the ability to transact must stop now.

### 2. Inventory open commitments

List every open order, invoice, claim, credit and forecast, and disposition each one individually.

### 3. Revoke access and settle data

Remove portal and system access, and have the DPO determine the disposition of every record — including those under hold.

### 4. Notify and close

Communicate the outcome, the final settlement position and what the supplier must do.

### 5. Attest

Record who did what, and confirm no post-termination transactions occurred.

## Outputs

- Blocked status
- Resolved commitments
- Data disposition record
- Offboarding attestation

## Quality bar

No supplier can transact after termination, every open commitment has a disposition, and every record has a retention decision.

## Anti-patterns

- Resolving payments and data first, and blocking last.
- Archiving the supplier record while leaving it transactable.
- Purging data that is under legal or contractual hold.

# Payment Release

> **skills_payment_release** · checklist · version 1.0.0

How to release a payment safely: scheduling, discount capture, independent bank verification, dual control and reconciliation.

---

## When to use this skill

Before every payment run.

## Prerequisites

- Approved invoices
- Verified supplier banking data
- Dual control in place

## Method

### 1. Schedule the run

Group approved invoices, apply discount deadlines and contractual terms, and confirm the cash position.

### 2. Verify banking data

Confirm the destination account is the verified account, through a channel independent of any recent change request.

### 3. Check holds and flags

Exclude every invoice under a hold, a fraud flag or an unresolved exception.

### 4. Obtain dual authorisation

Two named people authorise the run. An agent may prepare and summarise the run; it may never authorise it.

### 5. Release, remit and reconcile

Release the file, send remittance advice, and reconcile the confirmation back to the ledger the same day.

## Outputs

- Payment run
- Bank verification record
- Reconciliation record

## Quality bar

Every payment can be traced to an approved invoice, a verified bank account and a named release authorisation. Any of the three missing means it does not run.

## Anti-patterns

- Releasing payments for suppliers whose bank data changed recently without independent verification.
- Running payments for invoices still on hold.
- Assuming a failed payment file simply needs resubmitting.

# Purchase Order Creation

> **skills_po_creation** · howto · version 1.0.0

How to build a purchase order that is complete on issue — every field a supplier needs to act, and every field a matcher needs to reconcile.

---

## When to use this skill

When creating or amending a purchase order.

## Prerequisites

- Approved requisition
- Contract pricing
- Complete supplier and material master data

## Method

### 1. Build from the approved requisition

Line items, quantities and the cost centre come from the requisition. Do not re-derive them.

### 2. Apply contract pricing

Pull the price, currency, unit of measure, payment terms and validity from the contract. Record the price source.

### 3. Complete the commercial fields

Delivery address, contact, delivery date, tax treatment, freight terms and any service start date.

### 4. Validate

Run completeness and policy validation. Blocking validation failures stop the order; warnings are reviewed.

### 5. Issue and confirm

Issue the order, transmit it to the supplier, and monitor for acknowledgement.

## Outputs

- Issued purchase order
- PO validation results

## Quality bar

The supplier can act on the order without a phone call, and the accounts payable matcher can reconcile it against a receipt without a query.

## Anti-patterns

- Free-text descriptions instead of item references.
- Leaving delivery dates blank and relying on a separate email.
- Omitting unit of measure or currency on a multi-currency order.

# Procurement Portfolio Analysis

> **skills_portfolio_analysis** · analysis · version 1.0.0

How to read the spend cube and turn it into a procurement portfolio view: concentration, tail spend, maverick spend, category volatility and the structural signals that drive strategy.

---

## When to use this skill

At the start of strategy work, whenever a category boundary is questioned, and whenever the organisation needs to know where its leverage actually is.

## Prerequisites

- A 12-month spend cube
- An agreed category taxonomy

## Method

### 1. Establish the baseline

Reconcile the spend cube to the finance ledger for the period. Discrepancies above 0.5% are resolved before analysis begins.

### 2. Map concentration

Compute the share of spend with the top one, five and ten suppliers per category, and the share held by suppliers with no contract.

### 3. Segment the tail

Quantify transactions below the sourcing threshold. High tail share means the process, not the suppliers, is the problem.

### 4. Detect maverick spend

Identify spend with suppliers outside the approved panel, and spend above contract price for contracted suppliers.

### 5. Read volatility

Examine month-to-month and year-on-year variation. Volatile categories need different sourcing levers than stable ones — aggregation versus direct negotiation.

## Outputs

- Concentration analysis by category and supplier
- Tail and maverick spend quantification
- Volatility and trend indicators

## Quality bar

Every figure is traceable to the spend cube and reproducible. Totals reconcile to finance. A number that cannot be reproduced is not in the analysis.

## Anti-patterns

- Analysing supplier names rather than categories, because the taxonomy is uncomfortable.
- Mixing periods or currencies without restating, producing a trend that is an artefact.
- Reporting category share without the absolute value behind it.

# Process Improvement Design

> **skills_process_improvement** · howto · version 1.0.0

How to turn operational evidence into a framework change: identify the friction, size the benefit, design the change across every artefact it touches, and validate before publishing.

---

## When to use this skill

When cycle times miss target, when exception rates are high, or when a framework release is being prepared.

## Prerequisites

- Process telemetry available
- Named process owner engaged

## Method

### 1. Find the friction

Locate the step where time is actually spent, not where people believe it is spent. Compare telemetry against the exception narrative.

### 2. Size it

Quantify the cost of the current state — cycle time, effort, exceptions, leakage — so the benefit can be compared against the effort.

### 3. Design the whole change

Specify the change to the process object, the skill, the policy and the template. A half-change produces the wrong behaviour.

### 4. Validate

Pilot with a real volume of work, with the practitioner who will do it. Watch the step, do not ask about it.

### 5. Publish

Release through the co-design governance, then measure against the baseline you captured.

## Outputs

- Improvement proposal
- Change set across process, skill, policy and template
- Pilot evidence

## Quality bar

The proposal names every artefact it touches. A change to a process step alone is rejected as incomplete.

## Anti-patterns

- Improving the documentation of a process without changing the process.
- Declaring a benefit without a measurement point and a baseline.
- Changing a process without changing the template that implements it.

# Requirement Analysis

> **skills_requirement_analysis** · playbook · version 1.0.0

How to convert a business need into a specification precise enough to source, evaluate and contract against without further clarification.

---

## When to use this skill

Before drafting an RFx, when a request is returned for correction, and when evaluation criteria are defined.

## Prerequisites

- A qualified, budgeted requirement
- The relevant category strategy

## Method

### 1. Separate need from solution

State the business outcome the requirement serves before describing any product or service.

### 2. Make it testable

Express each requirement so that a bid can be scored against it and a delivered item can be checked against it.

### 3. Cover the whole lifecycle

Include implementation, service levels, support, training, end-of-life and data obligations. These are where the cost is usually hidden.

### 4. Define the criteria now

Draft the evaluation criteria and weighting at the same time as the specification, before any supplier is approached.

### 5. Sanity-check for ambiguity

Have someone outside the project read it. Ask them to tell you what would win. That is your criteria.

## Outputs

- Requirements specification
- Draft evaluation criteria

## Quality bar

Two independent evaluators, given only the specification, would reach the same conclusion about which bid is better.

## Anti-patterns

- Writing the requirement around a preferred supplier's product.
- Leaving evaluation criteria implicit so they can be adjusted later.
- Ignoring the service and support requirements because the price is the headline.
